# landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/

## Expand description

Landlock is a security feature available since Linux 5.13.
The goal is to enable to restrict ambient rights
(e.g., global filesystem access)
for a set of processes by creating safe security sandboxes as new security layers
in addition to the existing system-wide access-controls.
This kind of sandbox is expected to help mitigate the security impact of bugs,
unexpected or malicious behaviors in applications.
Landlock empowers any process, including unprivileged ones, to securely restrict themselves.
More information about Landlock can be found in the [official website](https://landlock.io).

This crate provides a safe abstraction for the Landlock system calls, along with some helpers.

Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV): 1.71

[§](https://landlock.io#use-cases)Use cases

This crate is especially useful to protect users’ data by sandboxing:

- trusted applications dealing with potentially malicious data (e.g., complex file format, network request) that could exploit security vulnerabilities;
- sandbox managers, container runtimes or shells launching untrusted applications.

[§](https://landlock.io#examples)Examples

A simple example can be found with the [ path_beneath_rules()](https://landlock.io/fn.path_beneath_rules.html) helper.
More complex examples can be found with the

[and the](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html)

`Ruleset` documentation[sandboxer example](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/rust-landlock/blob/master/examples/sandboxer.rs).

[§](https://landlock.io#current-limitations)Current limitations

This crate exposes the Landlock features available as of Linux 6.15 (Landlock [ABI v7](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V7))
and then inherits some [kernel limitations](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/landlock.html#current-limitations)
that will be addressed with future kernel releases
(e.g., arbitrary mounts are always denied).

[§](https://landlock.io#compatibility)Compatibility

Types defined in this crate are designed to enable the strictest Landlock configuration
for the given kernel on which the program runs.
In the default [best-effort](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.BestEffort) mode,
[ Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html) will determine compatibility
with the intersection of the currently running kernel’s features
and those required by the caller.
This way, callers can distinguish between
Landlock compatibility issues inherent to the current system
(e.g., file names that don’t exist)
and misconfiguration that should be fixed in the program
(e.g., empty or inconsistent access rights).

[identifies such kind of errors.](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)

`RulesetError`With [ set_compatibility(CompatLevel::BestEffort)](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility),
users of the crate may mark Landlock features that are deemed required
and other features that may be downgraded to use lower security on systems
where they can’t be enforced.
It is discouraged to compare the system’s provided

[Landlock ABI](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html)version directly, as it is difficult to track detailed ABI differences which are handled thanks to the

[trait.](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html)

`Compatible`To make it easier to migrate to a new version of this library,
we use the builder pattern
and designed objects to require the minimal set of method arguments.
Most `enum` are marked as `non_exhaustive` to enable backward-compatible evolutions.

[§](https://landlock.io#test-strategy)Test strategy

Developers should test their sandboxed applications
with a kernel that supports all requested Landlock features
and check that [ RulesetCreated::restrict_self()](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html#method.restrict_self) returns a status matching

[to make sure everything works as expected in an enforced sandbox. Alternatively, using](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictionStatus.html)

`Ok(RestrictionStatus { ruleset: RulesetStatus::FullyEnforced, no_new_privs: true, })`[will immediately inform about unsupported Landlock features. These configurations should only depend on the test environment (e.g.](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility)

`set_compatibility(CompatLevel::HardRequirement)`[by checking an environment variable](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/rust-landlock/search?q=LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI)). However, applications should only check that no error is returned (i.e.

`Ok(_)`)
and optionally log and inform users that the application is not fully sandboxed
because of missing features from the running kernel.[§](https://landlock.io#audit-logging)Audit logging

Landlock ABI v7 adds control over audit logging through boolean setters, especially
[ log_new_exec()](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html#method.log_new_exec)) which is useful (but noisy) for sandboxer
tools.

## Macros[§](https://landlock.io#macros)

- [make_](https://landlock.io/macro.make_bitflags.html)- bitflags
- `make_bitflags!`provides a succint syntax for creating instances of- `BitFlags<T>`. Instead of repeating the name of your type for each flag you want to add, try- `make_bitflags!(Flags::{Foo | Bar})`.

## Structs[§](https://landlock.io#structs)

- [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)
- Represents a set of flags of some type `T`.`T`must have the`#[bitflags]`attribute applied.
- [Errno](https://landlock.io/struct.Errno.html)
- Get the underlying errno value.
- [NetPort](https://landlock.io/struct.NetPort.html)
- Landlock rule for a network port.
- [Path](https://landlock.io/struct.PathBeneath.html)- Beneath
- Landlock rule for a file hierarchy.
- [PathFd](https://landlock.io/struct.PathFd.html)
- Simple helper to open a file or a directory with the `O_PATH`flag.
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html)- Self
- Builder for calling `landlock_restrict_self()`without creating a Landlock domain.
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelfStatus.html)- Self - Status
- Status returned by `RestrictSelf::apply()`
- [Restriction](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictionStatus.html)- Status
- Status of a `RulesetCreated``restrict_self()`
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html)
- Landlock ruleset builder.
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html)- Created
- Ruleset created with `Ruleset::create()`

## Enums[§](https://landlock.io#enums)

- [ABI](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html)
- Version of the Landlock [ABI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_binary_interface).
- [Access](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessError.html)- Error
- [Access](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html)- Fs
- File system access right.
- [Access](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessNet.html)- Net
- Network access right.
- [AddRule](https://landlock.io/enum.AddRuleError.html)- Error
- Identifies errors when adding a rule to a ruleset.
- [AddRules](https://landlock.io/enum.AddRulesError.html)- Error
- Identifies errors when adding rules to a ruleset thanks to an iterator returning Result<Rule, E> items.
- [Compat](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatError.html)- Error
- [Compat](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html)- Level
- See the `Compatible`
- [Create](https://landlock.io/enum.CreateRulesetError.html)- Ruleset - Error
- Identifies errors when creating a ruleset.
- [Erratum](https://landlock.io/enum.Erratum.html)
- Fixed kernel issues for the running Landlock implementation.
- [Handle](https://landlock.io/enum.HandleAccessError.html)- Access - Error
- Identifies errors when updating the ruleset’s handled access-rights.
- [Handle](https://landlock.io/enum.HandleAccessesError.html)- Accesses - Error
- [Landlock](https://landlock.io/enum.LandlockStatus.html)- Status
- Status of Landlock support for the running system.
- [Path](https://landlock.io/enum.PathBeneathError.html)- Beneath - Error
- [Path](https://landlock.io/enum.PathFdError.html)- FdError
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/enum.RestrictSelfError.html)- Self - Error
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/enum.RestrictSelfFlag.html)- Self - Flag
- Identifies a configuration flag for the `landlock_restrict_self()`syscall.
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)- Error
- Maps to all errors that can be returned by a ruleset action.
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetStatus.html)- Status
- Enforcement status of a ruleset.
- [Scope](https://landlock.io/enum.Scope.html)
- Scope right.
- [Scope](https://landlock.io/enum.ScopeError.html)- Error
- Identifies errors when updating the ruleset’s scopes.
- [Syscall](https://landlock.io/enum.SyscallFlagError.html)- Flag - Error
- Identifies errors when configuring a syscall flag.

## Traits[§](https://landlock.io#traits)

- [Access](https://landlock.io/trait.Access.html)
- [Compatible](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html)
- Properly handles runtime unsupported features.
- [Handled](https://landlock.io/trait.HandledAccess.html)- Access
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/trait.RestrictSelfAttr.html)- Self - Attr
- Trait for types that accept restrict_self flag configuration.
- [Rule](https://landlock.io/trait.Rule.html)
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetAttr.html)- Attr
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html)- Created - Attr
- [Syscall](https://landlock.io/trait.SyscallFlag.html)- Flag
- Marker trait for syscall flag types used in compatibility checks.

## Functions[§](https://landlock.io#functions)

- [path_](https://landlock.io/fn.path_beneath_rules.html)- beneath_ - rules
- Helper to quickly create an iterator of PathBeneath rules.

# Landlock: Unprivileged Sandboxing &#8212; Landlock  documentation

Source: https://landlock.io

# Landlock: Unprivileged Sandboxing[#](https://landlock.io#landlock-unprivileged-sandboxing)

The goal of Landlock is to enable restricting ambient rights (e.g. global filesystem access) for a set of processes. Because Landlock is a stackable LSM, it makes it possible to create safe security sandboxes as new security layers in addition to the existing system-wide access controls. This kind of sandbox is expected to help mitigate the security impact of bugs or unexpected/malicious behaviors in user space applications. Landlock empowers any process, including unprivileged ones, to securely restrict themselves.

## Resources[#](https://landlock.io#resources)

Main resources are available through the left panel.

Additional resources:

## Contribute[#](https://landlock.io#contribute)

Kernel development happens on the [Linux Security Modules mailing list](https://lore.kernel.org/linux-security-module/)
by [submitting patches](https://docs.kernel.org/process/submitting-patches.html).

User space news is on the [Landlock mailing list](https://lore.kernel.org/landlock/).
You can [subscribe](mailto:landlock+subscribe%40lists.linux.dev) and
[post](mailto:landlock%40lists.linux.dev) with any email client.

# landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/index.html

## Expand description

Landlock is a security feature available since Linux 5.13.
The goal is to enable to restrict ambient rights
(e.g., global filesystem access)
for a set of processes by creating safe security sandboxes as new security layers
in addition to the existing system-wide access-controls.
This kind of sandbox is expected to help mitigate the security impact of bugs,
unexpected or malicious behaviors in applications.
Landlock empowers any process, including unprivileged ones, to securely restrict themselves.
More information about Landlock can be found in the [official website](https://landlock.io).

This crate provides a safe abstraction for the Landlock system calls, along with some helpers.

Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV): 1.71

[§](https://landlock.io#use-cases)Use cases

This crate is especially useful to protect users’ data by sandboxing:

- trusted applications dealing with potentially malicious data (e.g., complex file format, network request) that could exploit security vulnerabilities;
- sandbox managers, container runtimes or shells launching untrusted applications.

[§](https://landlock.io#examples)Examples

A simple example can be found with the [ path_beneath_rules()](https://landlock.io/fn.path_beneath_rules.html) helper.
More complex examples can be found with the

[and the](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html)

`Ruleset` documentation[sandboxer example](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/rust-landlock/blob/master/examples/sandboxer.rs).

[§](https://landlock.io#current-limitations)Current limitations

This crate exposes the Landlock features available as of Linux 6.15 (Landlock [ABI v7](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V7))
and then inherits some [kernel limitations](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/landlock.html#current-limitations)
that will be addressed with future kernel releases
(e.g., arbitrary mounts are always denied).

[§](https://landlock.io#compatibility)Compatibility

Types defined in this crate are designed to enable the strictest Landlock configuration
for the given kernel on which the program runs.
In the default [best-effort](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.BestEffort) mode,
[ Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html) will determine compatibility
with the intersection of the currently running kernel’s features
and those required by the caller.
This way, callers can distinguish between
Landlock compatibility issues inherent to the current system
(e.g., file names that don’t exist)
and misconfiguration that should be fixed in the program
(e.g., empty or inconsistent access rights).

[identifies such kind of errors.](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)

`RulesetError`With [ set_compatibility(CompatLevel::BestEffort)](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility),
users of the crate may mark Landlock features that are deemed required
and other features that may be downgraded to use lower security on systems
where they can’t be enforced.
It is discouraged to compare the system’s provided

[Landlock ABI](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html)version directly, as it is difficult to track detailed ABI differences which are handled thanks to the

[trait.](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html)

`Compatible`To make it easier to migrate to a new version of this library,
we use the builder pattern
and designed objects to require the minimal set of method arguments.
Most `enum` are marked as `non_exhaustive` to enable backward-compatible evolutions.

[§](https://landlock.io#test-strategy)Test strategy

Developers should test their sandboxed applications
with a kernel that supports all requested Landlock features
and check that [ RulesetCreated::restrict_self()](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html#method.restrict_self) returns a status matching

[to make sure everything works as expected in an enforced sandbox. Alternatively, using](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictionStatus.html)

`Ok(RestrictionStatus { ruleset: RulesetStatus::FullyEnforced, no_new_privs: true, })`[will immediately inform about unsupported Landlock features. These configurations should only depend on the test environment (e.g.](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility)

`set_compatibility(CompatLevel::HardRequirement)`[by checking an environment variable](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/rust-landlock/search?q=LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI)). However, applications should only check that no error is returned (i.e.

`Ok(_)`)
and optionally log and inform users that the application is not fully sandboxed
because of missing features from the running kernel.[§](https://landlock.io#audit-logging)Audit logging

Landlock ABI v7 adds control over audit logging through boolean setters, especially
[ log_new_exec()](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html#method.log_new_exec)) which is useful (but noisy) for sandboxer
tools.

## Macros[§](https://landlock.io#macros)

- [make_](https://landlock.io/macro.make_bitflags.html)- bitflags
- `make_bitflags!`provides a succint syntax for creating instances of- `BitFlags<T>`. Instead of repeating the name of your type for each flag you want to add, try- `make_bitflags!(Flags::{Foo | Bar})`.

## Structs[§](https://landlock.io#structs)

- [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)
- Represents a set of flags of some type `T`.`T`must have the`#[bitflags]`attribute applied.
- [Errno](https://landlock.io/struct.Errno.html)
- Get the underlying errno value.
- [NetPort](https://landlock.io/struct.NetPort.html)
- Landlock rule for a network port.
- [Path](https://landlock.io/struct.PathBeneath.html)- Beneath
- Landlock rule for a file hierarchy.
- [PathFd](https://landlock.io/struct.PathFd.html)
- Simple helper to open a file or a directory with the `O_PATH`flag.
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html)- Self
- Builder for calling `landlock_restrict_self()`without creating a Landlock domain.
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelfStatus.html)- Self - Status
- Status returned by `RestrictSelf::apply()`
- [Restriction](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictionStatus.html)- Status
- Status of a `RulesetCreated``restrict_self()`
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html)
- Landlock ruleset builder.
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html)- Created
- Ruleset created with `Ruleset::create()`

## Enums[§](https://landlock.io#enums)

- [ABI](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html)
- Version of the Landlock [ABI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_binary_interface).
- [Access](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessError.html)- Error
- [Access](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html)- Fs
- File system access right.
- [Access](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessNet.html)- Net
- Network access right.
- [AddRule](https://landlock.io/enum.AddRuleError.html)- Error
- Identifies errors when adding a rule to a ruleset.
- [AddRules](https://landlock.io/enum.AddRulesError.html)- Error
- Identifies errors when adding rules to a ruleset thanks to an iterator returning Result<Rule, E> items.
- [Compat](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatError.html)- Error
- [Compat](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html)- Level
- See the `Compatible`
- [Create](https://landlock.io/enum.CreateRulesetError.html)- Ruleset - Error
- Identifies errors when creating a ruleset.
- [Erratum](https://landlock.io/enum.Erratum.html)
- Fixed kernel issues for the running Landlock implementation.
- [Handle](https://landlock.io/enum.HandleAccessError.html)- Access - Error
- Identifies errors when updating the ruleset’s handled access-rights.
- [Handle](https://landlock.io/enum.HandleAccessesError.html)- Accesses - Error
- [Landlock](https://landlock.io/enum.LandlockStatus.html)- Status
- Status of Landlock support for the running system.
- [Path](https://landlock.io/enum.PathBeneathError.html)- Beneath - Error
- [Path](https://landlock.io/enum.PathFdError.html)- FdError
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/enum.RestrictSelfError.html)- Self - Error
- [Restrict](https://landlock.io/enum.RestrictSelfFlag.html)- Self - Flag
- Identifies a configuration flag for the `landlock_restrict_self()`syscall.
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)- Error
- Maps to all errors that can be returned by a ruleset action.
- [Ruleset](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetStatus.html)- Status
- Enforcement status of a ruleset.
- [Scope](https://landlock.io/enum.Scope.html)
- Scope right.
- [Scope](https://landlock.io/enum.ScopeError.html)- Error
- Identifies errors when updating the ruleset’s scopes.
- [Syscall](https://landlock.io/enum.SyscallFlagError.html)- Flag - Error
- Identifies errors when configuring a syscall flag.

## Traits[§](https://landlock.io#traits)

[138](https://landlock.io#138)    impl Sealed for crate::AccessNet {}

[142](https://landlock.io#142)
[143](https://landlock.io#143)#[cfg(test)]
[144](https://landlock.io#144)mod tests {
[145](https://landlock.io#145)    use crate::*;
[146](https://landlock.io#146)
[147](https://landlock.io#147)    // These integration tests exercise the full builder-to-syscall path via
[148](https://landlock.io#148)    // check_ruleset_support().  Other tests in compat.rs and errata.rs make
[149](https://landlock.io#149)    // read-only kernel queries (LandlockStatus::current(), Erratum::current())
[150](https://landlock.io#150)    // but do not create rulesets or restrict threads.  All remaining tests use
[151](https://landlock.io#151)    // Ruleset::from(ABI) to exercise the builder logic and compatibility
[152](https://landlock.io#152)    // engine without kernel interaction.
[153](https://landlock.io#153)
[154](https://landlock.io#154)    // Emulate old kernel supports.  Iterates each ABI variant, mocks the
[155](https://landlock.io#155)    // builder via B::from(abi), runs the closure on a dedicated thread, and
[156](https://landlock.io#156)    // dispatches to the caller's assertion closures based on whether the
[157](https://landlock.io#157)    // mocked ABI is emulatable on the running kernel.
[158](https://landlock.io#158)    fn check_support<B, S, F, OkFn, ErrFn>(
[159](https://landlock.io#159)        partial: ABI,
[160](https://landlock.io#160)        full: Option<ABI>,
[161](https://landlock.io#161)        check: F,
[162](https://landlock.io#162)        assert_ok: OkFn,
[163](https://landlock.io#163)        assert_err: ErrFn,
[164](https://landlock.io#164)    ) where
[165](https://landlock.io#165)        B: From<ABI> + Send + 'static,
[166](https://landlock.io#166)        F: Fn(B) -> Result<S, TestRulesetError> + Send + Copy + 'static,
[167](https://landlock.io#167)        S: std::fmt::Debug + Send + 'static,
[168](https://landlock.io#168)        OkFn: Fn(ABI, Result<S, TestRulesetError>),
[169](https://landlock.io#169)        ErrFn: Fn(Result<S, TestRulesetError>),
[170](https://landlock.io#170)    {
[171](https://landlock.io#171)        // If there is no partial support, it means that `full == partial`.
[172](https://landlock.io#172)        assert!(partial <= full.unwrap_or(partial));
[173](https://landlock.io#173)        for abi in ABI::iter() {
[174](https://landlock.io#174)            // Ensures restrict_self() is called on a dedicated thread to avoid inconsistent tests.
[175](https://landlock.io#175)            let ret = std::thread::spawn(move || check(B::from(abi)))
[176](https://landlock.io#176)                .join()
[177](https://landlock.io#177)                .unwrap();
[178](https://landlock.io#178)
[179](https://landlock.io#179)            // Useful for failed tests and with cargo test -- --show-output
[180](https://landlock.io#180)            println!("Checking ABI {abi:?}: received {ret:#?}");
[181](https://landlock.io#181)            if can_emulate(abi, partial, full) {
[182](https://landlock.io#182)                assert_ok(abi, ret);
[183](https://landlock.io#183)            } else {
[184](https://landlock.io#184)                assert_err(ret);
[185](https://landlock.io#185)            }
[186](https://landlock.io#186)        }
[187](https://landlock.io#187)    }
[188](https://landlock.io#188)
[189](https://landlock.io#189)    fn check_ruleset_support<F>(
[190](https://landlock.io#190)        partial: ABI,
[191](https://landlock.io#191)        full: Option<ABI>,
[192](https://landlock.io#192)        check: F,
[193](https://landlock.io#193)        error_if_abi_lt_partial: bool,
[194](https://landlock.io#194)    ) where
[195](https://landlock.io#195)        F: Fn(Ruleset) -> Result<RestrictionStatus, TestRulesetError> + Send + Copy + 'static,
[196](https://landlock.io#196)    {
[197](https://landlock.io#197)        check_support(
[198](https://landlock.io#198)            partial,
[199](https://landlock.io#199)            full,
[200](https://landlock.io#200)            check,
[201](https://landlock.io#201)            |abi, ret| {
[202](https://landlock.io#202)                if abi < partial && error_if_abi_lt_partial {
[203](https://landlock.io#203)                    // TODO: Check exact error type; this may require better error types.
[204](https://landlock.io#204)                    assert!(matches!(ret, Err(TestRulesetError::Ruleset(_))));
[205](https://landlock.io#205)                } else {
[206](https://landlock.io#206)                    let full_support = if let Some(full_inner) = full {
[207](https://landlock.io#207)                        abi >= full_inner
[208](https://landlock.io#208)                    } else {
[209](https://landlock.io#209)                        false
[210](https://landlock.io#210)                    };
[211](https://landlock.io#211)                    let ruleset_status = if full_support {
[212](https://landlock.io#212)                        RulesetStatus::FullyEnforced
[213](https://landlock.io#213)                    } else if abi >= partial {
[214](https://landlock.io#214)                        RulesetStatus::PartiallyEnforced
[215](https://landlock.io#215)                    } else {
[216](https://landlock.io#216)                        RulesetStatus::NotEnforced
[217](https://landlock.io#217)                    };
[218](https://landlock.io#218)                    let landlock_status = abi.into();
[219](https://landlock.io#219)                    println!("Expecting ruleset status {ruleset_status:?}");
[220](https://landlock.io#220)                    println!("Expecting Landlock status {landlock_status:?}");
[221](https://landlock.io#221)                    assert!(matches!(
[222](https://landlock.io#222)                        ret,
[223](https://landlock.io#223)                        Ok(RestrictionStatus {
[224](https://landlock.io#224)                            ruleset,
[225](https://landlock.io#225)                            landlock,
[226](https://landlock.io#226)                            no_new_privs: true,
[227](https://landlock.io#227)                            ..
[228](https://landlock.io#228)                        }) if ruleset == ruleset_status && landlock == landlock_status
[229](https://landlock.io#229)                    ))
[230](https://landlock.io#230)                }
[231](https://landlock.io#231)            },
[232](https://landlock.io#232)            |ret| {
[233](https://landlock.io#233)                // The errno value should be ENOSYS, EOPNOTSUPP, EINVAL (e.g. when an unknown
[234](https://landlock.io#234)                // access right is provided), or E2BIG (e.g. when there is an unknown field in a
[235](https://landlock.io#235)                // Landlock syscall attribute).
[236](https://landlock.io#236)                let errno = get_errno_from_landlock_status();
[237](https://landlock.io#237)                println!("Expecting error {errno:?}");
[238](https://landlock.io#238)                match ret {
[239](https://landlock.io#239)                    Err(
[240](https://landlock.io#240)                        ref error @ TestRulesetError::Ruleset(RulesetError::CreateRuleset(
[241](https://landlock.io#241)                            CreateRulesetError::CreateRulesetCall { ref source },
[242](https://landlock.io#242)                        )),
[243](https://landlock.io#243)                    ) => {
[244](https://landlock.io#244)                        assert_eq!(source.raw_os_error(), Some(*Errno::from(error)));
[245](https://landlock.io#245)                        match (source.raw_os_error(), errno) {
[246](https://landlock.io#246)                            (Some(e1), Some(e2)) => assert_eq!(e1, e2),
[247](https://landlock.io#247)                            (Some(e1), None) => assert!(matches!(e1, libc::EINVAL | libc::E2BIG)),
[248](https://landlock.io#248)                            _ => unreachable!(),
[249](https://landlock.io#249)                        }
[250](https://landlock.io#250)                    }
[251](https://landlock.io#251)                    // restrict_self flags may be rejected by the kernel with EINVAL
[252](https://landlock.io#252)                    // when the mock ABI is higher than the running kernel's ABI.
[253](https://landlock.io#253)                    Err(TestRulesetError::Ruleset(RulesetError::RestrictSelf(
[254](https://landlock.io#254)                        RestrictSelfError::RestrictSelfCall { ref source },
[255](https://landlock.io#255)                    ))) => {
[256](https://landlock.io#256)                        assert_eq!(source.raw_os_error(), Some(libc::EINVAL));
[257](https://landlock.io#257)                    }
[258](https://landlock.io#258)                    _ => unreachable!(),
[259](https://landlock.io#259)                }
[260](https://landlock.io#260)            },
[261](https://landlock.io#261)        );
[262](https://landlock.io#262)    }
[263](https://landlock.io#263)
[264](https://landlock.io#264)    // Emulate old kernel supports for the domain-less RestrictSelf builder.
[265](https://landlock.io#265)    //
[266](https://landlock.io#266)    // Unlike check_ruleset_support, RestrictSelf does not create a Landlock domain, so there is no
[267](https://landlock.io#267)    // ruleset enforcement status to assert.  We verify the kernel probe (status.landlock) and
[268](https://landlock.io#268)    // propagate any syscall error.  RestrictSelf::apply() enforces PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS by default.
[269](https://landlock.io#269)    fn check_restrict_self_support<F>(partial: ABI, full: Option<ABI>, check: F)
[270](https://landlock.io#270)    where
[271](https://landlock.io#271)        F: Fn(RestrictSelf) -> Result<RestrictSelfStatus, TestRulesetError> + Send + Copy + 'static,
[272](https://landlock.io#272)    {
[273](https://landlock.io#273)        check_support(
[274](https://landlock.io#274)            partial,
[275](https://landlock.io#275)            full,
[276](https://landlock.io#276)            check,
[277](https://landlock.io#277)            |abi, ret| {
[278](https://landlock.io#278)                let landlock_status: LandlockStatus = abi.into();
[279](https://landlock.io#279)                println!("Expecting Landlock status {landlock_status:?}");
[280](https://landlock.io#280)                assert!(matches!(
[281](https://landlock.io#281)                    ret,
[282](https://landlock.io#282)                    Ok(RestrictSelfStatus { landlock, .. }) if landlock == landlock_status
[283](https://landlock.io#283)                ));
[284](https://landlock.io#284)            },
[285](https://landlock.io#285)            |ret| {
[286](https://landlock.io#286)                // The errno value should be ENOSYS, EOPNOTSUPP, or EINVAL (e.g. when actual_flags
[287](https://landlock.io#287)                // carries bits unknown to the running kernel).  Unlike check_ruleset_support,
[288](https://landlock.io#288)                // landlock_restrict_self() is the first syscall here, so ENOSYS is possible when
[289](https://landlock.io#289)                // Landlock is unavailable.
[290](https://landlock.io#290)                let errno = get_errno_from_landlock_status();
[291](https://landlock.io#291)                println!("Expecting error {errno:?}");
[292](https://landlock.io#292)                match ret {
[293](https://landlock.io#293)                    Err(
[294](https://landlock.io#294)                        ref error @ TestRulesetError::Ruleset(RulesetError::RestrictSelf(
[295](https://landlock.io#295)                            RestrictSelfError::RestrictSelfCall { ref source },
[296](https://landlock.io#296)                        )),
[297](https://landlock.io#297)                    ) => {
[298](https://landlock.io#298)                        assert_eq!(source.raw_os_error(), Some(*Errno::from(error)));
[299](https://landlock.io#299)                        match (source.raw_os_error(), errno) {
[300](https://landlock.io#300)                            (Some(e1), Some(e2)) => assert_eq!(e1, e2),
[301](https://landlock.io#301)                            (Some(e1), None) => assert!(matches!(e1, libc::EINVAL | libc::E2BIG)),
[302](https://landlock.io#302)                            _ => unreachable!(),
[303](https://landlock.io#303)                        }
[304](https://landlock.io#304)                    }
[305](https://landlock.io#305)                    _ => unreachable!(),
[306](https://landlock.io#306)                }
[307](https://landlock.io#307)            },
[308](https://landlock.io#308)        );
[309](https://landlock.io#309)    }
[310](https://landlock.io#310)
[311](https://landlock.io#311)    #[test]

[316](https://landlock.io#316)            abi,
[317](https://landlock.io#317)            Some(abi),
[318](https://landlock.io#318)            move |ruleset: Ruleset| -> _ {
[319](https://landlock.io#319)                Ok(ruleset
[320](https://landlock.io#320)                    .handle_access(AccessFs::from_all(abi))?
[321](https://landlock.io#321)                    .create()?
[322](https://landlock.io#322)                    .add_rule(PathBeneath::new(PathFd::new("/")?, AccessFs::from_all(abi)))?
[323](https://landlock.io#323)                    .restrict_self()?)
[324](https://landlock.io#324)            },
[325](https://landlock.io#325)            false,
[326](https://landlock.io#326)        );

[390](https://landlock.io#390)    fn allow_root_fragile() {
[391](https://landlock.io#391)        let abi = ABI::V1;
[392](https://landlock.io#392)
[393](https://landlock.io#393)        check_ruleset_support(
[394](https://landlock.io#394)            abi,
[395](https://landlock.io#395)            Some(abi),
[396](https://landlock.io#396)            move |ruleset: Ruleset| -> _ {
[397](https://landlock.io#397)                // Sets default support requirement: abort the whole sandboxing for any Landlock error.
[398](https://landlock.io#398)                Ok(ruleset
[399](https://landlock.io#399)                    // Must have at least the execute check…
[400](https://landlock.io#400)                    .set_compatibility(CompatLevel::HardRequirement)
[401](https://landlock.io#401)                    .handle_access(AccessFs::Execute)?
[402](https://landlock.io#402)                    // …and possibly others.
[403](https://landlock.io#403)                    .set_compatibility(CompatLevel::BestEffort)
[404](https://landlock.io#404)                    .handle_access(AccessFs::from_all(abi))?
[405](https://landlock.io#405)                    .create()?
[406](https://landlock.io#406)                    .no_new_privs(true)
[407](https://landlock.io#407)                    .add_rule(PathBeneath::new(PathFd::new("/")?, AccessFs::from_all(abi)))?
[408](https://landlock.io#408)                    .restrict_self()?)
[409](https://landlock.io#409)            },
[410](https://landlock.io#410)            true,
[411](https://landlock.io#411)        );
[412](https://landlock.io#412)    }

[517](https://landlock.io#517)    fn abi_v5_ioctl_dev() {
[518](https://landlock.io#518)        check_ruleset_support(
[519](https://landlock.io#519)            ABI::V4,
[520](https://landlock.io#520)            Some(ABI::V5),
[521](https://landlock.io#521)            move |ruleset: Ruleset| -> _ {
[522](https://landlock.io#522)                Ok(ruleset
[523](https://landlock.io#523)                    .handle_access(AccessNet::BindTcp)?

# path_beneath_rules in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/fn.path_beneath_rules.html

```
pub fn path_beneath_rules<I, P, A>(
    paths: I,
    access: A,
) -> impl
```
[Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html)<Item = [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[PathBeneath](https://landlock.io/struct.PathBeneath.html)<[PathFd](https://landlock.io/struct.PathFd.html)>, [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>>## Expand description

Helper to quickly create an iterator of PathBeneath rules.

[§](https://landlock.io#note)Note

From the kernel’s perspective, Landlock rules operate on file descriptors, not paths.
This is a helper to create rules based on paths. Here, `path_beneath_rules()` silently ignores
paths that cannot be opened, hence making the obtainment of a file descriptor impossible. When
possible and for a given path, `path_beneath_rules()` automatically adjusts [access rights](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html),
depending on whether a directory or a file is present at that said path.

This behavior is the result of [ CompatLevel::BestEffort](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.BestEffort), which is the default compatibility level of
all created rulesets. Thus, it applies to the example below. However, if

[is set using](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.HardRequirement)

`CompatLevel::HardRequirement`[, attempting to create an incompatible rule at runtime will cause this crate to raise an error instead.](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility)

`Compatible::set_compatibility`[§](https://landlock.io#example)Example

```
use landlock::{
    ABI, Access, AccessFs, Ruleset, RulesetAttr, RulesetCreatedAttr, RulesetStatus, RulesetError,
    path_beneath_rules,
};
fn restrict_thread() -> Result<(), RulesetError> {
    let abi = ABI::V1;
    let status = Ruleset::default()
        .handle_access(AccessFs::from_all(abi))?
        .create()?
        // Read-only access to /usr, /etc and /dev.
        .add_rules(path_beneath_rules(&["/usr", "/etc", "/dev"], AccessFs::from_read(abi)))?
        // Read-write access to /home and /tmp.
        .add_rules(path_beneath_rules(&["/home", "/tmp"], AccessFs::from_all(abi)))?
        .restrict_self()?;
    match status.ruleset {
        // The FullyEnforced case must be tested by the developer.
        RulesetStatus::FullyEnforced => println!("Fully sandboxed."),
        RulesetStatus::PartiallyEnforced => println!("Partially sandboxed."),
        // Users should be warned that they are not protected.
        RulesetStatus::NotEnforced => println!("Not sandboxed! Please update your kernel."),
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

# Ruleset in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/struct.Ruleset.html

`pub struct Ruleset { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Landlock ruleset builder.

`Ruleset` enables to create a Landlock ruleset in a flexible way
following the builder pattern.
Most build steps return a [ Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html) with

[.](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)

`RulesetError`You should probably not create more than one ruleset per application. Creating multiple rulesets is only useful when gradually restricting an application (e.g., a first set of generic restrictions before reading any file, then a second set of tailored restrictions after reading the configuration).

[§](https://landlock.io#simple-example)Simple example

Simple helper handling only Landlock-related errors.

```
use landlock::{
    Access, AccessFs, PathBeneath, PathFd, RestrictionStatus, Ruleset, RulesetAttr,
    RulesetCreatedAttr, RulesetError, ABI,
};
use std::os::unix::io::AsFd;
fn restrict_fd<T>(hierarchy: T) -> Result<RestrictionStatus, RulesetError>
where
    T: AsFd,
{
    // The Landlock ABI should be incremented (and tested) regularly.
    let abi = ABI::V1;
    let access_all = AccessFs::from_all(abi);
    let access_read = AccessFs::from_read(abi);
    Ok(Ruleset::default()
        .handle_access(access_all)?
        .create()?
        .add_rule(PathBeneath::new(hierarchy, access_read))?
        .restrict_self()?)
}
let fd = PathFd::new("/home").expect("failed to open /home");
let status = restrict_fd(fd).expect("failed to build the ruleset");
```
[§](https://landlock.io#generic-example)Generic example

More generic helper handling a set of file hierarchies
and multiple types of error (i.e. [ RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)
and

[.](https://landlock.io/enum.PathFdError.html)

`PathFdError````
use landlock::{
    Access, AccessFs, PathBeneath, PathFd, PathFdError, RestrictionStatus, Ruleset,
    RulesetAttr, RulesetCreatedAttr, RulesetError, ABI,
};
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
enum MyRestrictError {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Ruleset(#[from] RulesetError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    AddRule(#[from] PathFdError),
}
fn restrict_paths(hierarchies: &[&str]) -> Result<RestrictionStatus, MyRestrictError> {
    // The Landlock ABI should be incremented (and tested) regularly.
    let abi = ABI::V1;
    let access_all = AccessFs::from_all(abi);
    let access_read = AccessFs::from_read(abi);
    Ok(Ruleset::default()
        .handle_access(access_all)?
        .create()?
        .add_rules(
            hierarchies
                .iter()
                .map::<Result<_, MyRestrictError>, _>(|p| {
                    Ok(PathBeneath::new(PathFd::new(p)?, access_read))
                }),
        )?
        .restrict_self()?)
}
let status = restrict_paths(&["/usr", "/home"]).expect("failed to build the ruleset");
```

# ABI in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.ABI.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum ABI {
    Unsupported = 0,
    V1 = 1,
    V2 = 2,
    V3 = 3,
    V4 = 4,
    V5 = 5,
    V6 = 6,
    V7 = 7,
}
```
## Expand description

Version of the Landlock [ABI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_binary_interface).

`ABI` enables getting the features supported by a specific Landlock ABI
(without relying on the kernel version which may not be accessible or patched).
For example, [ AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V1)](https://landlock.io/trait.Access.html#tymethod.from_all)
gets all the file system access rights defined by the first version.

Without `ABI`, it would be hazardous to rely on the the full set of access flags
(e.g., `BitFlags::<AccessFs>::all()` or `BitFlags::ALL`),
a moving target that would change the semantics of your Landlock rule
when migrating to a newer version of this crate.
Indeed, a simple `cargo update` or `cargo install` run by any developer
can result in a new version of this crate (fixing bugs or bringing non-breaking changes).
This crate cannot give any guarantee concerning the new restrictions resulting from
these unknown bits (i.e. access rights) that would not be controlled by your application but by
a future version of this crate instead.
Because we cannot know what the effect on your application of an unknown restriction would be
when handling an untested Landlock access right (i.e. denied-by-default access),
it could trigger bugs in your application.

This crate provides a set of tools to sandbox as much as possible
while guaranteeing a consistent behavior thanks to the [ Compatible](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html) methods.
You should also test with different relevant kernel versions,
see

[landlock-test-tools](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/landlock-test-tools)and

[CI integration](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/rust-landlock/pull/41).

This way, we can have the guarantee that the use of a set of tested Landlock ABI works as
expected because features brought by newer Landlock ABI will never be enabled by default
(cf. [Linux kernel compatibility contract](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#compatibility)).

In a nutshell, test the access rights you request on a kernel that support them and on a kernel that doesn’t support them.

Derived `Debug` formats are [not stable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/fmt/trait.Debug.html#stability).

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

### Unsupported = 0

Kernel not supporting Landlock, either because it is not built with Landlock or Landlock is not enabled at boot.

### V7 = 7

## Trait Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#trait-implementations)

An erratum is applicable if the ABI includes the feature affected by the bug.
For example, [ Erratum::TcpSocketIdentification](https://landlock.io/enum.Erratum.html#variant.TcpSocketIdentification) is only applicable to

[and later, since TCP access rights were introduced in that version.](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V4)

`ABI::V4`Uses the same incremental accumulation pattern as
[ AccessFs::from_write()](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html#method.from_write).

[§](https://landlock.io#stability)Stability

The set of errata returned for a given ABI may grow in future versions of this crate as new kernel bug fixes are identified and backported. Do not rely on the exact set being stable across crate versions.

# CompatLevel in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.CompatLevel.html

```
pub enum CompatLevel {
    BestEffort,
    SoftRequirement,
    HardRequirement,
}
```
## Variants[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.BestEffort)

### BestEffort

Takes into account the build requests if they are supported by the running system, or silently ignores them otherwise. Never returns a compatibility error.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.SoftRequirement)

### SoftRequirement

Takes into account the build requests if they are supported by the running system,
or silently ignores the whole build object otherwise.
Never returns a compatibility error.
If not supported,
the call to [ RulesetCreated::restrict_self()](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html#method.restrict_self)
will return a

[.](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictionStatus.html)

`RestrictionStatus { ruleset: RulesetStatus::NotEnforced, no_new_privs: false, }`[§](https://landlock.io#variant.HardRequirement)

### HardRequirement

# Compatible in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/trait.Compatible.html

`pub trait Compatible: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) + OptionCompatLevelMut {
    // Provided methods
    fn [set_compatibility](https://landlock.io#method.set_compatibility)(self, level: [CompatLevel](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html)) -> Self { ... }
[set_best_effort](https://landlock.io#method.set_best_effort)(self, best_effort: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> Self
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) { ... }
}## Expand description

Properly handles runtime unsupported features.

This guarantees consistent behaviors across crate users and runtime kernels even if this crate get new features. It eases backward compatibility and enables future-proofness.

Landlock is a security feature designed to help improve security of a running system thanks to application developers. To protect users as much as possible, compatibility with the running system should then be handled in a best-effort way, contrary to common system features. In some circumstances (e.g. applications carefully designed to only be run with a specific set of kernel features), it may be required to error out if some of these features are not available and will then not be enforced.

## Provided Methods[§](https://landlock.io#provided-methods)

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/compat.rs.html#637-640)#### fn [set_compatibility](https://landlock.io#method.set_compatibility)(self, level: [CompatLevel](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html)) -> Self

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/compat.rs.html#637-640)

#### fn [set_compatibility](https://landlock.io#method.set_compatibility)(self, level: [CompatLevel](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html)) -> Self

To enable a best-effort security approach,
Landlock features that are not supported by the running system
are silently ignored by default,
which is a sane choice for most use cases.
However, on some rare circumstances,
developers may want to have some guarantees that their applications
will not run if a certain level of sandboxing is not possible.
If we really want to error out when not all our requested requirements are met,
then we can configure it with `set_compatibility()`.

The `Compatible` trait is implemented for all object builders
(e.g. [ Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html)).
Such builders have a set of methods to incrementally build an object.
These build methods rely on kernel features that may not be available at runtime.
The

`set_compatibility()` method enables to control the effect of
the following build method calls starting after the `set_compatibility()` call.
Such effect can be:- to silently ignore unsupported features
and continue building (`CompatLevel::BestEffort`
- to silently ignore unsupported features
and ignore the whole build (`CompatLevel::SoftRequirement`
- to return an error for any unsupported feature (`CompatLevel::HardRequirement`

Taking [ Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html) as an example,
the

[build method returns a](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetAttr.html#method.handle_access)

`handle_access()`[that can be](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`[with a nested](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)

`Err(RulesetError)`[. Such error can only occur with a running Linux kernel not supporting the requested Landlock accesses](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatError.html)

`CompatError`*and*if the current compatibility level is

[. However, such error is not possible with](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.HardRequirement)

`CompatLevel::HardRequirement`[nor](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.BestEffort)

`CompatLevel::BestEffort`[.](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.SoftRequirement)

`CompatLevel::SoftRequirement`The order of this call is important because
it defines the behavior of the following build method calls that return a [ Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html).
If

`set_compatibility(CompatLevel::HardRequirement)` is called on an object,
then a [may be returned for the next method calls, until the next call to](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatError.html)

`CompatError``set_compatibility()`.
This enables to change the behavior of a set of build method calls,
for instance to be sure that the sandbox will at least restrict some access rights.New objects inherit the compatibility configuration of their parents, if any.
For instance, [ Ruleset::create()](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html#method.create) returns
a

[object that inherits the](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html)

`RulesetCreated``Ruleset`’s compatibility configuration.[§](https://landlock.io#example-with-softrequirement)Example with `SoftRequirement`

Let’s say an application legitimately needs to rename files between directories.
Because of [previous Landlock limitations](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#file-renaming-and-linking-abi-2),
this was forbidden with the [first version of Landlock](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V1),
but it is now handled starting with the [second version](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V2).
For this use case, we only want the application to be sandboxed
if we have the guarantee that it will not break a legitimate usage (i.e. rename files).
We then create a ruleset which will either support file renaming
(thanks to [ AccessFs::Refer](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html#variant.Refer)) or silently do nothing.

```
use landlock::*;
fn ruleset_handling_renames() -> Result<RulesetCreated, RulesetError> {
    Ok(Ruleset::default()
        // This ruleset must either handle the AccessFs::Refer right,
        // or it must silently ignore the whole sandboxing.
        .set_compatibility(CompatLevel::SoftRequirement)
        .handle_access(AccessFs::Refer)?
        // However, this ruleset may also handle other (future) access rights
        // if they are supported by the running kernel.
        .set_compatibility(CompatLevel::BestEffort)
        .handle_access(AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V7))?
        .create()?)
}
```
[§](https://landlock.io#example-with-hardrequirement)Example with `HardRequirement`

Security-dedicated applications may want to ensure that
an untrusted software component is subject to a minimum of restrictions before launching it.
In this case, we want to create a ruleset which will at least support
all restrictions provided by the [first version of Landlock](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V1),
and opportunistically handle restrictions supported by newer kernels.

```
use landlock::*;
fn ruleset_fragile() -> Result<RulesetCreated, RulesetError> {
    Ok(Ruleset::default()
        // This ruleset must either handle at least all accesses defined by
        // the first Landlock version (e.g. AccessFs::WriteFile),
        // or the following handle_access() call must return a wrapped
        // AccessError<AccessFs>::Incompatible error.
        .set_compatibility(CompatLevel::HardRequirement)
        .handle_access(AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V1))?
        // However, this ruleset may also handle new access rights
        // (e.g. AccessFs::Refer defined by the second version of Landlock)
        // if they are supported by the running kernel,
        // but without returning any error otherwise.
        .set_compatibility(CompatLevel::BestEffort)
        .handle_access(AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V7))?
        .create()?)
}
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://landlock.io#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# RulesetCreated in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/struct.RulesetCreated.html

`pub struct RulesetCreated { /* private fields */ }`## Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#implementations)

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/ruleset.rs.html#913-966)#### pub fn [restrict_self](https://landlock.io#method.restrict_self)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RestrictionStatus](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictionStatus.html), [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/ruleset.rs.html#913-966)

#### pub fn [restrict_self](https://landlock.io#method.restrict_self)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RestrictionStatus](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictionStatus.html), [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>

Attempts to restrict the calling thread with the ruleset
according to the best-effort configuration
(see [ RulesetCreated::set_compatibility()](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html#method.set_compatibility) and

[). Call](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.BestEffort)

`CompatLevel::BestEffort``prctl(2)` with the `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`
according to the ruleset configuration.On error, returns a wrapped [ RestrictSelfError](https://landlock.io/enum.RestrictSelfError.html).

}## Provided Methods[§](https://landlock.io#provided-methods)

Attempts to add a set of new rules to the ruleset.

On error, returns a (double) wrapped [ AddRulesError](https://landlock.io/enum.AddRulesError.html).

[§](https://landlock.io#example)Example

Create a custom iterator to read paths from environment variable.

```
use landlock::{
    Access, AccessFs, BitFlags, PathBeneath, PathFd, PathFdError, RestrictionStatus, Ruleset,
    RulesetAttr, RulesetCreatedAttr, RulesetError, ABI,
};
use std::env;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::{OsStrExt, OsStringExt};
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
enum PathEnvError<'a> {
    #[error(transparent)]
    Ruleset(#[from] RulesetError),
    #[error(transparent)]
    AddRuleIter(#[from] PathFdError),
    #[error("missing environment variable {0}")]
    MissingVar(&'a str),
}
struct PathEnv {
    paths: Vec<u8>,
    access: BitFlags<AccessFs>,
}
impl PathEnv {
    // env_var is the name of an environment variable
    // containing paths requested to be allowed.
    // Paths are separated with ":", e.g. "/bin:/lib:/usr:/proc".
    // In case an empty string is provided,
    // no restrictions are applied.
    // `access` is the set of access rights allowed for each of the parsed paths.
    fn new<'a>(
        env_var: &'a str, access: BitFlags<AccessFs>
    ) -> Result<Self, PathEnvError<'a>> {
        Ok(Self {
            paths: env::var_os(env_var)
                .ok_or(PathEnvError::MissingVar(env_var))?
                .into_vec(),
            access,
        })
    }
    fn iter(
        &self,
    ) -> impl Iterator<Item = Result<PathBeneath<PathFd>, PathEnvError<'static>>> + '_ {
        let is_empty = self.paths.is_empty();
        self.paths
            .split(|b| *b == b':')
            // Skips the first empty element from of an empty string.
            .skip_while(move |_| is_empty)
            .map(OsStr::from_bytes)
            .map(move |path|
                Ok(PathBeneath::new(PathFd::new(path)?, self.access)))
    }
}
fn restrict_env() -> Result<RestrictionStatus, PathEnvError<'static>> {
    Ok(Ruleset::default()
        .handle_access(AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V1))?
        .create()?
        // In the shell: export EXECUTABLE_PATH="/usr:/bin:/sbin"
        .add_rules(PathEnv::new("EXECUTABLE_PATH", AccessFs::Execute.into())?.iter())?
        .restrict_self()?)
}
```

Configures the ruleset to call `prctl(2)` with the `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS` command
in [ restrict_self()](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html#method.restrict_self).

This `prctl(2)` call is never ignored, even if an error was encountered on a [ Ruleset](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html) or

[method call while](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html)

`RulesetCreated`[was set.](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.SoftRequirement)

`CompatLevel::SoftRequirement`[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/ruleset.rs.html#855-858)#### fn [log_same_exec](https://landlock.io#method.log_same_exec)(self, set: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>

Controls logging of denied accesses for the creating thread and its children
running the same executable (before `execve(2)`).
Logging is **enabled** by default.  See
[kernel documentation](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#enforcing-a-ruleset).

Calling with `false` sets the `LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SAME_EXEC_OFF` flag.
Calling with `true` is a no-op (the default behavior).

This setter only applies when restricting with a domain.

On error, returns a wrapped
[ SyscallFlagError<RestrictSelfFlag>](https://landlock.io/enum.SyscallFlagError.html).

# make_bitflags in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/macro.make_bitflags.html

# Macro make_bitflags

```
macro_rules! make_bitflags {
    ( $enum:ident ::{ $($variant:ident)|* } ) => { ... };
    ( $enum:ident :: $variant:ident ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

`make_bitflags!` provides a succint syntax for creating instances of
`BitFlags<T>`. Instead of repeating the name of your type for each flag
you want to add, try `make_bitflags!(Flags::{Foo | Bar})`.

```
let x = make_bitflags!(Test::{A | C});
assert_eq!(x, Test::A | Test::C);
// Also works in const contexts:
const X: BitFlags<Test> = make_bitflags!(Test::A);
```

---

# BitFlags in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/struct.BitFlags.html

# Struct BitFlags

`pub struct BitFlags<T, N = <T as RawBitFlags>::Numeric> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Represents a set of flags of some type `T`.
`T` must have the `#[bitflags]` attribute applied.

A `BitFlags<T>` is as large as the `T` itself,
and stores one flag per bit.

[§](https://landlock.io#comparison-operators-partialord-and-ord)Comparison operators, `PartialOrd``Ord`

`PartialOrd``Ord`To make it possible to use `BitFlags` as the key of a
[`BTreeMap`][std::collections::BTreeMap], `BitFlags` implements
[ Ord](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/cmp/trait.Ord.html). There is no meaningful total order for bitflags,
so the implementation simply compares the integer values of the bits.

Unfortunately, this means that comparing `BitFlags` with an operator
like `<=` will compile, and return values that are probably useless
and not what you expect. In particular, `<=` does *not* check whether
one value is a subset of the other. Use [ BitFlags::contains](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.contains) for that.

[§](https://landlock.io#customizing-default)Customizing `Default`

By default, creating an instance of `BitFlags<T>` with `Default` will result
in an empty set. If that’s undesirable, you may customize this:

```
#[bitflags(default = B | C)]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
enum MyFlag {
    A = 0b0001,
    B = 0b0010,
    C = 0b0100,
    D = 0b1000,
}
assert_eq!(BitFlags::default(), MyFlag::B | MyFlag::C);
```
[§](https://landlock.io#memory-layout)Memory layout

`BitFlags<T>` is marked with the `#[repr(transparent)]` trait, meaning
it can be safely transmuted into the corresponding numeric type.

Usually, the same can be achieved by using [ BitFlags::bits](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.bits) in one
direction, and

[,](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits)

`BitFlags::from_bits`[, or](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits_truncate)

`BitFlags::from_bits_truncate`[in the other direction. However, transmuting might still be useful if, for example, you’re dealing with an entire array of](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits_unchecked)

`BitFlags::from_bits_unchecked``BitFlags`.When transmuting *into* a `BitFlags`, make sure that each set bit
corresponds to an existing flag
(cf. [ from_bits_unchecked](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits_unchecked)).

For example:

```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)] // <-- the repr determines the numeric type
#[derive(Copy, Clone)]
enum TransmuteMe {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
}
// NOTE: we use a small, self-contained function to handle the slice
// conversion to make sure the lifetimes are right.
fn transmute_slice<'a>(input: &'a [BitFlags<TransmuteMe>]) -> &'a [u8] {
    unsafe {
        slice::from_raw_parts(input.as_ptr() as *const u8, input.len())
    }
}
let many_flags = &[
    TransmuteMe::One.into(),
    TransmuteMe::One | TransmuteMe::Two,
];
let as_nums = transmute_slice(many_flags);
assert_eq!(as_nums, &[0b01, 0b11]);
```
[§](https://landlock.io#implementation-notes)Implementation notes

You might expect this struct to be defined as

Ideally, that would be the case. However, because `const fn`s cannot
have trait bounds in current Rust, this would prevent us from providing
most `const fn` APIs. As a workaround, we define `BitFlags` with two
type parameters, with a default for the second one:

Manually providing a type for the `N` type parameter shouldn’t ever
be necessary.

The types substituted for `T` and `N` must always match, creating a
`BitFlags` value where that isn’t the case is only possible with
incorrect unsafe code.

## Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#implementations)

#### pub const unsafe fn [from_bits_unchecked_c](https://landlock.io#method.from_bits_unchecked_c)(

    const_token: ConstToken<T, [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html)>,

Create a new BitFlags unsafely, without checking if the bits form a valid bit pattern for the type.

Const variant of
[ from_bits_unchecked](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits_unchecked).

Consider using
[ from_bits_truncate_c](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits_truncate_c) instead.

[§](https://landlock.io#safety)Safety

All bits set in `val` must correspond to a value of the enum.

#### pub const fn [from_bits_truncate_c](https://landlock.io#method.from_bits_truncate_c)(
    bits: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html),
    const_token: ConstToken<T, [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html)>,

#### pub const fn [from_bits_truncate_c](https://landlock.io#method.from_bits_truncate_c)(
    bits: [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html),
    const_token: ConstToken<T, [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html)>,

Create a `BitFlags<T>` from an underlying bitwise value. If any
invalid bits are set, ignore them.

```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MyFlag {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
    Three = 1 << 2,
}
const FLAGS: BitFlags<MyFlag> =
    BitFlags::<MyFlag>::from_bits_truncate_c(0b10101010, BitFlags::CONST_TOKEN);
assert_eq!(FLAGS, MyFlag::Two);
```
Bitwise OR — return value contains flag if either argument does.

Also available as `a | b`, but operator overloads are not usable
in `const fn`s at the moment.

#### pub const fn [intersection_c](https://landlock.io#method.intersection_c)(self, other: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T, [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html)>) -> [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T, [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html)>

#### pub const fn [intersection_c](https://landlock.io#method.intersection_c)(self, other: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T, [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html)>) -> [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T, [u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.u8.html)>

Bitwise AND — return value contains flag if both arguments do.

Also available as `a & b`, but operator overloads are not usable
in `const fn`s at the moment.

Bitwise NOT — return value contains flag if argument doesn’t.

Also available as `!a`, but operator overloads are not usable
in `const fn`s at the moment.

Moreover, due to `const fn` limitations, `not_c` needs a
[`ConstToken`] as an argument.

```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MyFlag {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
    Three = 1 << 2,
}
const FLAGS: BitFlags<MyFlag> = make_bitflags!(MyFlag::{One | Two});
const NEGATED: BitFlags<MyFlag> = FLAGS.not_c(BitFlags::CONST_TOKEN);
assert_eq!(NEGATED, MyFlag::Three);
```
Create a `BitFlags` if the raw value provided does not contain
any illegal flags.

See also: [a convenience re-export in the `BitFlag` trait][BitFlag::from_bits],
which can help avoid the need for type hints.

```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
enum MyFlag {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
    Three = 1 << 2,
}
let flags: BitFlags<MyFlag> = BitFlags::from_bits(0b11).unwrap();
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::One), true);
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::Two), true);
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::Three), false);
let invalid = BitFlags::<MyFlag>::from_bits(1 << 3);
assert!(invalid.is_err());
```
#### pub fn [from_bits_truncate](https://landlock.io#method.from_bits_truncate)(bits: <T as RawBitFlags>::Numeric) -> [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>

#### pub fn [from_bits_truncate](https://landlock.io#method.from_bits_truncate)(bits: <T as RawBitFlags>::Numeric) -> [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>

Create a `BitFlags` from an underlying bitwise value. If any
invalid bits are set, ignore them.

See also: [a convenience re-export in the `BitFlag` trait][BitFlag::from_bits_truncate],
which can help avoid the need for type hints.

```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MyFlag {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
    Three = 1 << 2,
}
let flags: BitFlags<MyFlag> = BitFlags::from_bits_truncate(0b1_1011);
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::One), true);
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::Two), true);
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::Three), false);
```
#### pub unsafe fn [from_bits_unchecked](https://landlock.io#method.from_bits_unchecked)(
    val: <T as RawBitFlags>::Numeric,
) -> [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>

#### pub unsafe fn [from_bits_unchecked](https://landlock.io#method.from_bits_unchecked)(
    val: <T as RawBitFlags>::Numeric,
) -> [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>

Create a new BitFlags unsafely, without checking if the bits form a valid bit pattern for the type.

Consider using [ from_bits](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits)
or

[instead.](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#method.from_bits_truncate)

`from_bits_truncate`[§](https://landlock.io#safety-1)Safety

All bits set in `val` must correspond to a value of the enum.

[§](https://landlock.io#example)Example

```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MyFlag {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
    Three = 1 << 2,
}
let flags: BitFlags<MyFlag> = unsafe {
    BitFlags::from_bits_unchecked(0b011)
};
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::One), true);
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::Two), true);
assert_eq!(flags.contains(MyFlag::Three), false);
```
Create a `BitFlags` with no flags set (in other words, with a value of `0`).

See also: [`BitFlag::empty`], a convenience reexport;
[ BitFlags::EMPTY](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#associatedconstant.EMPTY), the same functionality available
as a constant for

`const fn` code.```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MyFlag {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
    Three = 1 << 2,
}
let empty: BitFlags<MyFlag> = BitFlags::empty();
assert!(empty.is_empty());
assert_eq!(empty.contains(MyFlag::One), false);
assert_eq!(empty.contains(MyFlag::Two), false);
assert_eq!(empty.contains(MyFlag::Three), false);
```
Create a `BitFlags` with all flags set.

See also: [`BitFlag::all`], a convenience reexport;
[ BitFlags::ALL](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html#associatedconstant.ALL), the same functionality available
as a constant for

`const fn` code.```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum MyFlag {
    One = 1 << 0,
    Two = 1 << 1,
    Three = 1 << 2,
}
let empty: BitFlags<MyFlag> = BitFlags::all();
assert!(empty.is_all());
assert_eq!(empty.contains(MyFlag::One), true);
assert_eq!(empty.contains(MyFlag::Two), true);
assert_eq!(empty.contains(MyFlag::Three), true);
```
#### pub fn [bits](https://landlock.io#method.bits)(self) -> <T as RawBitFlags>::Numeric

#### pub fn [bits](https://landlock.io#method.bits)(self) -> <T as RawBitFlags>::Numeric

Returns the underlying bitwise value.

```
#[bitflags]
#[repr(u8)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Flags {
    Foo = 1 << 0,
    Bar = 1 << 1,
}
let both_flags = Flags::Foo | Flags::Bar;
assert_eq!(both_flags.bits(), 0b11);
```
Inserts if `cond` holds, else removes

```
#[bitflags]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[repr(u8)]
enum MyFlag {
    A = 1 << 0,
    B = 1 << 1,
    C = 1 << 2,
}
let mut state = MyFlag::A | MyFlag::C;
state.set(MyFlag::A | MyFlag::B, false);
// Because the condition was false, both
// `A` and `B` are removed from the set
assert_eq!(state, MyFlag::C);
```
## Trait Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#trait-implementations)

An erratum is applicable if the ABI includes the feature affected by the bug.
For example, [ Erratum::TcpSocketIdentification](https://landlock.io/enum.Erratum.html#variant.TcpSocketIdentification) is only applicable to

[and later, since TCP access rights were introduced in that version.](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V4)

`ABI::V4`Uses the same incremental accumulation pattern as
[ AccessFs::from_write()](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html#method.from_write).

[§](https://landlock.io#stability)Stability

The set of errata returned for a given ABI may grow in future versions of this crate as new kernel bug fixes are identified and backported. Do not rely on the exact set being stable across crate versions.

#### fn [set_compatibility](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility)(self, level: [CompatLevel](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html)) -> Self

To enable a best-effort security approach,
Landlock features that are not supported by the running system
are silently ignored by default,
which is a sane choice for most use cases.
However, on some rare circumstances,
developers may want to have some guarantees that their applications
will not run if a certain level of sandboxing is not possible.
If we really want to error out when not all our requested requirements are met,
then we can configure it with

`set_compatibility()`. [Read more](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility)[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/net.rs.html#228)[§](https://landlock.io#impl-Compatible-for-NetPort)### impl [Compatible](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html) for [NetPort](https://landlock.io/struct.NetPort.html)

# PathFd in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/struct.PathFd.html

`pub struct PathFd { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Simple helper to open a file or a directory with the `O_PATH` flag.

This is the recommended way to identify a path
and manage the lifetime of the underlying opened file descriptor.
Indeed, using other [ AsFd](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/os/fd/owned/trait.AsFd.html) implementations such as

[brings more complexity and may lead to unexpected errors (e.g., denied access).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/fs/struct.File.html)

`File`[§](https://landlock.io#example)Example

```
use landlock::{AccessFs, PathBeneath, PathFd, PathFdError};
fn allowed_root_dir(access: AccessFs) -> Result<PathBeneath<PathFd>, PathFdError> {
    let fd = PathFd::new("/")?;
    Ok(PathBeneath::new(fd, access))
}
```

# RestrictSelf in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/struct.RestrictSelf.html

`pub struct RestrictSelf { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Builder for calling `landlock_restrict_self()` without creating a
Landlock domain.

Use this when you want to configure `landlock_restrict_self()` flags
without creating a ruleset or a Landlock domain (e.g., muting
subdomain audit logs for nested domains).

Only [ log_subdomains()](https://landlock.io/trait.RestrictSelfAttr.html#method.log_subdomains) is available
on this builder.  Domain-specific setters
(

[,](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html#method.log_same_exec)

`log_same_exec()`[) require a Landlock domain via](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html#method.log_new_exec)

`log_new_exec()`[.](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html)

`RulesetCreated`Available since Landlock [ABI v7](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V7).

`no_new_privs` is enforced by default; call
[ no_new_privs(false)](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html#method.no_new_privs) to opt out.

[§](https://landlock.io#example)Example

```
use landlock::*;
let status = RestrictSelf::default()
    .log_subdomains(false)?
    .apply()?;
println!("Landlock status: {:?}", status.landlock);
```
Use [ set_compatibility()](https://landlock.io/trait.Compatible.html#method.set_compatibility) to control
how unsupported flags are handled.

[ apply()](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html#method.apply) returns a

[with the Landlock support status and the effective flag states. Its name differs from](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelfStatus.html)

`RestrictSelfStatus`[to avoid the redundant](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html#method.restrict_self)

`RulesetCreated::restrict_self()``RestrictSelf::restrict_self()`.## Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#implementations)

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/restrict_self.rs.html#208-267)[§](https://landlock.io#impl-RestrictSelf)### impl [RestrictSelf](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html)

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/restrict_self.rs.html#208-267)

### impl [RestrictSelf](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html)

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/restrict_self.rs.html#217-220)

#### pub fn [no_new_privs](https://landlock.io#method.no_new_privs)(self, yes: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> Self

Configures whether to call `prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS)` during
[ apply()](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html#method.apply).  Defaults to

`true`.This `prctl(2)` call is never ignored, even if an error was
encountered while [ CompatLevel::SoftRequirement](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.SoftRequirement) was set.

See [ RestrictSelfAttr::log_subdomains()](https://landlock.io/trait.RestrictSelfAttr.html#method.log_subdomains) for compat-state
behavior when toggling this setter on unsupported kernels.

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/restrict_self.rs.html#233-266)#### pub fn [apply](https://landlock.io#method.apply)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RestrictSelfStatus](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelfStatus.html), [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/restrict_self.rs.html#233-266)

#### pub fn [apply](https://landlock.io#method.apply)(self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[RestrictSelfStatus](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelfStatus.html), [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>

Applies the configured restrict_self flags by calling
`landlock_restrict_self(-1, flags)`.

If `no_new_privs` is configured (default), also calls
`prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, 1, 0, 0, 0)` first, since the kernel
requires `no_new_privs` (or `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`) for
`landlock_restrict_self()`.  See
[ no_new_privs()](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html#method.no_new_privs) to opt out.

Returns a [ RestrictSelfStatus](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelfStatus.html) with the Landlock support status.
Skips the restrict_self syscall if no flags are enforceable.

# AccessError in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.AccessError.html

```
pub enum AccessError<T>{
    Empty,
    Unknown {
        access:
```
[BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>,
        unknown: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>,
    },
    Incompatible {
        access: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>,
    },
    PartiallyCompatible {
        access: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>,
        incompatible: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<T>,
    },
}## Variants[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Empty)

### Empty

The access-rights set is empty, which doesn’t make sense and would be rejected by the kernel.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Unknown)

### Unknown

The access-rights set was forged with the unsafe `BitFlags::from_bits_unchecked()` and it
contains unknown bits.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Incompatible)

### Incompatible

The best-effort approach was (deliberately) disabled and the requested access-rights are fully incompatible with the running kernel.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.PartiallyCompatible)

### PartiallyCompatible

The best-effort approach was (deliberately) disabled and the requested access-rights are partially incompatible with the running kernel.

## Trait Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#trait-implementations)
