# AccessFs in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.AccessFs.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]#[repr(u64)]pub enum AccessFs {
```
## Show 16 variants

    Execute = 1,
    WriteFile = 2,
    ReadFile = 4,
    ReadDir = 8,
    RemoveDir = 16,
    RemoveFile = 32,
    MakeChar = 64,
    MakeDir = 128,
    MakeReg = 256,
    MakeSock = 512,
    MakeFifo = 1_024,
    MakeBlock = 2_048,
    MakeSym = 4_096,
    Refer = 8_192,
    Truncate = 16_384,
    IoctlDev = 32_768,
}## Expand description

File system access right.

Each variant of `AccessFs` is an [access right](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/landlock.html#access-rights)
for the file system.
A set of access rights can be created with [ BitFlags<AccessFs>](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html).

[§](https://landlock.io#example)Example

```
use landlock::{ABI, Access, AccessFs, BitFlags, make_bitflags};
let exec = AccessFs::Execute;
let exec_set: BitFlags<AccessFs> = exec.into();
let file_content = make_bitflags!(AccessFs::{Execute | WriteFile | ReadFile});
let fs_v1 = AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V1);
let without_exec = fs_v1 & !AccessFs::Execute;
assert_eq!(fs_v1 | AccessFs::Refer, AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V2));
```
[§](https://landlock.io#warning)Warning

To avoid unknown restrictions **don’t use  BitFlags::<AccessFs>::all() nor BitFlags::ALL**,
but use a version you tested and vetted instead,
for instance

[. Direct use of](https://landlock.io/trait.Access.html#tymethod.from_all)

`AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V1)`**the**. See

[API is deprecated](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)`BitFlags`[for the rationale and help to test it.](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html)

`ABI`## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Execute)

### Execute = 1

Execute a file.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.WriteFile)

### WriteFile = 2

Open a file with write access.

[§](https://landlock.io#note)Note

Certain operations (such as [ std::fs::write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/fs/fn.write.html)) may also require

[since](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html#variant.Truncate)

`AccessFs::Truncate`[.](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V3)

`ABI::V3`[§](https://landlock.io#variant.ReadFile)

### ReadFile = 4

Open a file with read access.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.ReadDir)

### ReadDir = 8

Open a directory or list its content.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.RemoveDir)

### RemoveDir = 16

Remove an empty directory or rename one.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.RemoveFile)

### RemoveFile = 32

Unlink (or rename) a file.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.MakeChar)

### MakeChar = 64

Create (or rename or link) a character device.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.MakeDir)

### MakeDir = 128

Create (or rename) a directory.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.MakeReg)

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.MakeFifo)

Create (or rename or link) a block device.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.MakeSym)

### MakeSym = 4_096

Create (or rename or link) a symbolic link.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Refer)

### Refer = 8_192

Link or rename a file from or to a different directory.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Truncate)

### Truncate = 16_384

Truncate a file with `truncate(2)`, `ftruncate(2)`, `creat(2)`, or `open(2)` with `O_TRUNC`.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.IoctlDev)

### IoctlDev = 32_768

Send IOCL commands to a device file.

# AccessNet in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.AccessNet.html

Enum AccessNet   Copy item path  Source  #[non_exhaustive]

#[repr(u64)]

pub enum AccessNet {
    BindTcp = 1,
    ConnectTcp = 2,
}Expand description Network access right.

Each variant of `AccessNet` is an access right
for the network.
A set of access rights can be created with `BitFlags<AccessNet>`

§ Exampleuse  landlock::{ABI, Access, AccessNet, BitFlags, make_bitflags};
let  bind = AccessNet::BindTcp;
let  bind_set: BitFlags<AccessNet> = bind.into();
let  bind_connect = make_bitflags! (AccessNet::{BindTcp | ConnectTcp});
let  net_v4 = AccessNet::from_all(ABI::V4);
assert_eq! (bind_connect, net_v4);§ WarningTo avoid unknown restrictions don’t use `BitFlags::<AccessNet>::all()` nor `BitFlags::ALL` ,
but use a version you tested and vetted instead,
for instance `AccessNet::from_all(ABI::V4)`the `BitFlags` .
See `ABI`

# Erratum in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.Erratum.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]#[repr(u32)]pub enum Erratum {
    TcpSocketIdentification = 1,
    ScopedSignalHandling = 2,
    DisconnectedDirectoryHandling = 4,
}
```
## Expand description

Fixed kernel issues for the running Landlock implementation.

Each variant represents a specific bug fix that may have been
backported to the running kernel.  Use [ Erratum::current()](https://landlock.io/enum.Erratum.html#method.current)
before building a

[to decide which features are safe to use.](https://landlock.io/struct.Ruleset.html)

`Ruleset`An [ ABI](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html) version can be converted into the set of applicable errata
with

`BitFlags::<Erratum>::from(abi)`.[§](https://landlock.io#warning)Warning

Most applications should **not** check errata.  Disabling a sandboxing
feature because an erratum is not fixed could leave the system **less**
secure than using Landlock’s best-effort protection with the buggy
feature enabled.  Errata should only be used to **add** features
(e.g., enabling a restriction only when its bug is confirmed fixed),
never to remove them.

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.TcpSocketIdentification)

### TcpSocketIdentification = 1

Erratum 1 (ABI 4): non-TCP stream sockets (SMC, MPTCP, SCTP)
were incorrectly restricted by TCP access rights during
`bind(2)` and `connect(2)`.

Affects [ crate::AccessNet::BindTcp](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessNet.html#variant.BindTcp) and

[.](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessNet.html#variant.ConnectTcp)

`crate::AccessNet::ConnectTcp`See [erratum 1](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#erratum-1-tcp-socket-identification).

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.ScopedSignalHandling)

### ScopedSignalHandling = 2

Erratum 2 (ABI 6): signal scoping was overly restrictive, preventing sandboxed threads from signaling other threads within the same process in different domains.

Affects [ crate::Scope::Signal](https://landlock.io/enum.Scope.html#variant.Signal).

See [erratum 2](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#erratum-2-scoped-signal-handling).

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.DisconnectedDirectoryHandling)

### DisconnectedDirectoryHandling = 4

Erratum 3 (ABI 1): access rights could be widened through
rename or link actions on disconnected directories under
bind mounts, potentially bypassing `LANDLOCK_ACCESS_FS_REFER`
restrictions.

See [erratum 3](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#erratum-3-disconnected-directory-handling).

## Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://landlock.io#trait-implementations)

# LandlockStatus in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.LandlockStatus.html

```
pub enum LandlockStatus {
    NotEnabled,
    NotImplemented,
    Available {
        effective_abi:
```
[ABI](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html),
        kernel_abi: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.i32.html)>,
    },
}## Expand description

Status of Landlock support for the running system.

This enum is used to represent the status of the Landlock support for the system where the code is executed. It can indicate whether Landlock is available or not.

[§](https://landlock.io#warning)Warning

Sandboxed programs should only use this data to log or provide information to users,
not to change their behavior according to this status.  Indeed, the `Ruleset` and the other
types are designed to handle the compatibility in a simple and safe way.

## Variants[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.NotEnabled)

### NotEnabled

Landlock is supported but not enabled (`EOPNOTSUPP`).

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.NotImplemented)

### NotImplemented

Landlock is not implemented (i.e. not built into the running kernel: `ENOSYS`).

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Available)

### Available

Landlock is available and working on the running system.

This indicates that the kernel supports Landlock and it’s properly enabled.
The crate uses the `effective_abi` for all operations, which represents
the highest ABI version that both the kernel and this crate understand.

#### Fields

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Available.field.effective_abi)

`effective_abi: `[ABI](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html)The effective ABI version that this crate will use for Landlock operations. This is the intersection of what the kernel supports and what this crate knows about.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.Available.field.kernel_abi)

`kernel_abi: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.i32.html)>The actual kernel ABI version when it’s newer than any ABI supported by this crate.

If `Some(version)`, it means the running kernel supports Landlock ABI `version`
which is higher than the latest ABI known by this crate.

This field is purely informational and is never used for Landlock operations.
The crate always and only uses `effective_abi` for all functionality.

        access: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<[AccessFs](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html)>,
        incompatible: [BitFlags](https://landlock.io/struct.BitFlags.html)<[AccessFs](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html)>,
    },
}## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.StatCall)

### #[non_exhaustive]StatCall

To check that access-rights are consistent with a file descriptor, a call to
[ RulesetCreatedAttr::add_rule()](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html#method.add_rule)
looks at the file type with an

`fstat()` system call.#### Fields

## This variant is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.DirectoryAccess)

### DirectoryAccess

This error is returned by
[ RulesetCreatedAttr::add_rule()](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html#method.add_rule)
if the related PathBeneath object is not set to best-effort,
and if its allowed access-rights contain directory-only ones
whereas the file descriptor doesn’t point to a directory.

# RestrictSelfFlag in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.RestrictSelfFlag.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum RestrictSelfFlag {
    LogSameExec,
    LogNewExec,
    LogSubdomains,
}
```
## Expand description

Identifies a configuration flag for the `landlock_restrict_self()` syscall.

Unlike access rights ([ AccessFs](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessFs.html),

[) and scopes (](https://landlock.io/enum.AccessNet.html)

`AccessNet`[), these flags are not passed to](https://landlock.io/enum.Scope.html)

`Scope``landlock_create_ruleset()` but to `landlock_restrict_self()`.  They control
audit logging behavior rather than access restrictions.Each flag is set through a dedicated boolean method on
[ RulesetCreatedAttr](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html) or

[. The polarity mapping (e.g.,](https://landlock.io/trait.RestrictSelfAttr.html)

`RestrictSelfAttr``log_same_exec(false)` maps to `LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SAME_EXEC_OFF`)
is handled internally.## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

# RulesetStatus in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.RulesetStatus.html

```
pub enum RulesetStatus {
    FullyEnforced,
    PartiallyEnforced,
    NotEnforced,
}
```
## Expand description

Enforcement status of a ruleset.

## Variants[§](https://landlock.io#variants)

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.FullyEnforced)

### FullyEnforced

All requested restrictions are enforced.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.PartiallyEnforced)

### PartiallyEnforced

Some requested restrictions are enforced, following a best-effort approach.

[§](https://landlock.io#variant.NotEnforced)

### NotEnforced

The running system doesn’t support Landlock or a subset of the requested Landlock features.

# Scope in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/enum.Scope.html

use landlock::{ABI, Access, Scope, BitFlags, make_bitflags};
let signal = Scope::Signal;
let signal_set: BitFlags<Scope> = signal.into();
let signal_uds = make_bitflags!(Scope::{Signal | AbstractUnixSocket});
let scope_v6 = Scope::from_all(ABI::V6);
assert_eq!(signal_uds, scope_v6);

To avoid unknown restrictions don’t use BitFlags::<Scope>::all() nor BitFlags::ALL,
but use a version you tested and vetted instead,
for instance Scope::from_all(ABI::V6).
Direct use of the BitFlags API is deprecated.
See ABI for the rationale and help to test it.

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

If ABI <= ABI::V5, Scope::from_all() returns an empty BitFlags<AccessScope>, which
makes Ruleset::handle_access(AccessScope::from_all(ABI::V5)) return an error.

# RestrictSelfAttr in landlock - Rust

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/landlock/trait.RestrictSelfAttr.html

`pub trait RestrictSelfAttr: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) + RestrictSelfFlagsState {
    // Provided method
    fn [log_subdomains](https://landlock.io#method.log_subdomains)(self, set: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)> { ... }
}## Expand description

Trait for types that accept restrict_self flag configuration.

Provides [ log_subdomains()](https://landlock.io/trait.RestrictSelfAttr.html#method.log_subdomains) which works both
with and without a Landlock domain.

Implemented by [ RulesetCreated](https://landlock.io/struct.RulesetCreated.html) (via

[supertrait) and](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html)

`RulesetCreatedAttr`[.](https://landlock.io/struct.RestrictSelf.html)

`RestrictSelf`Domain-specific setters (`log_same_exec`, `log_new_exec`) are on
[ RulesetCreatedAttr](https://landlock.io/trait.RulesetCreatedAttr.html).

## Provided Methods[§](https://landlock.io#provided-methods)

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/restrict_self.rs.html#78-81)#### fn [log_subdomains](https://landlock.io#method.log_subdomains)(self, set: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>

[Source](https://landlock.io/src/landlock/restrict_self.rs.html#78-81)

#### fn [log_subdomains](https://landlock.io#method.log_subdomains)(self, set: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [RulesetError](https://landlock.io/enum.RulesetError.html)>

Controls logging of denied accesses from nested Landlock domains.
Logging is **enabled** by default.  See the
[kernel documentation](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#enforcing-a-ruleset).

Calling with `false` sets the `LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SUBDOMAINS_OFF` flag.
Setters are last-call-wins: calling again with a different boolean
re-configures the flag (e.g., `log_subdomains(false).log_subdomains(true)`
leaves logging enabled).

Setting to the default value never triggers a compatibility check,
so it cannot error even under
[ CompatLevel::HardRequirement](https://landlock.io/enum.CompatLevel.html#variant.HardRequirement)
on an unsupported kernel.

Available since Landlock [ABI v7](https://landlock.io/enum.ABI.html#variant.V7).

On error, returns a wrapped
[ SyscallFlagError<RestrictSelfFlag>](https://landlock.io/enum.SyscallFlagError.html).

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://landlock.io#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/1.96.0/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

Attempts to add a set of access rights that will be supported by this ruleset.
By default, all actions requiring these access rights will be denied.
Consecutive calls to `handle_access()` will be interpreted as logical ORs
with the previous handled accesses.

On error, returns a wrapped [ HandleAccessesError](https://landlock.io/enum.HandleAccessesError.html).
E.g.,

[155](#155)#[test]
[156](#156)fn consistent_access_fs_rw() {
[157](#157)    for abi in ABI::iter() {
[158](#158)        let access_all = AccessFs::from_all(abi);
[159](#159)        let access_read = AccessFs::from_read(abi);
[160](#160)        let access_write = AccessFs::from_write(abi);
[161](#161)        let access_file = AccessFs::from_file(abi);
[162](#162)        assert_eq!(access_read, !access_write & access_all);
[163](#163)        assert_eq!(access_read | access_write, access_all);
[164](#164)        assert_eq!(access_file, access_all & ACCESS_FILE);
[165](#165)    }

[191](#191)    fn into_add_rules_error(error: AddRuleError<Self>) -> AddRulesError {

[193](#193)    }
[194](#194)
[195](#195)    fn into_handle_accesses_error(error: HandleAccessError<Self>) -> HandleAccessesError {
[196](#196)        HandleAccessesError::Fs(error)
[197](#197)    }
[198](#198)}
[199](#199)
[200](#200)const ACCESS_FILE: BitFlags<AccessFs> = make_bitflags!(AccessFs::{
[203](#203)    ReadFile | WriteFile | Execute | Truncate | IoctlDev
[204](#204)});
[205](#205)
[206](#206)fn is_file<F>(fd: F) -> Result<bool, Error>
[208](#208)where
[209](#209)    F: AsFd,
[210](#210){
[211](#211)    unsafe {
[212](#212)        let mut stat = zeroed();
[213](#213)        match libc::fstat(fd.as_fd().as_raw_fd(), &mut stat) {
[214](#214)            0 => Ok((stat.st_mode & libc::S_IFMT) != libc::S_IFDIR),
[215](#215)            _ => Err(Error::last_os_error()),
[216](#216)        }
[217](#217)    }

[261](#261)impl<F> TryCompat<AccessFs> for PathBeneath<F>
[262](#262)where
[263](#263)    F: AsFd,
[264](#264){
[265](#265)    fn try_compat_children<L>(
[266](#266)        mut self,
[267](#267)        abi: ABI,
[268](#268)        parent_level: L,
[269](#269)        compat_state: &mut CompatState,
[270](#270)    ) -> Result<Option<Self>, CompatError<AccessFs>>
[271](#271)    where
[272](#272)        L: Into<CompatLevel>,
[273](#273)    {
[274](#274)        self.allowed_access = match self.allowed_access.try_compat(
[276](#276)            abi,
[277](#277)            self.tailored_compat_level(parent_level),
[278](#278)            compat_state,
[279](#279)        )? {
[280](#280)            Some(a) => a,
[281](#281)            None => return Ok(None),
[282](#282)        };
[283](#283)        Ok(Some(self))
[284](#284)    }
[285](#285)
[286](#286)    fn try_compat_inner(
[287](#287)        &mut self,
[288](#288)        _abi: ABI,
[289](#289)    ) -> Result<CompatResult<AccessFs>, CompatError<AccessFs>> {
[290](#290)        let valid_access =
[292](#292)            if is_file(&self.parent_fd).map_err(|e| PathBeneathError::StatCall { source: e })? {
[293](#293)                self.allowed_access & ACCESS_FILE
[294](#294)            } else {
[295](#295)                self.allowed_access
[296](#296)            };
[297](#297)
[298](#298)        if self.allowed_access != valid_access {
[299](#299)            let error = PathBeneathError::DirectoryAccess {
[300](#300)                access: self.allowed_access,
[301](#301)                incompatible: self.allowed_access ^ valid_access,
[302](#302)            }
[303](#303)            .into();
[304](#304)            self.allowed_access = valid_access;
[305](#305)            Ok(CompatResult::Partial(error))
[307](#307)        } else {
[308](#308)            Ok(CompatResult::Full)
[309](#309)        }
[310](#310)    }
[311](#311)}

[350](#350)fn path_beneath_try_compat() {
[351](#351)    use crate::*;
[352](#352)
[353](#353)    let abi = ABI::V1;
[354](#354)
[355](#355)    for file in &["/etc/passwd", "/dev/null"] {
[356](#356)        let mut compat_state = CompatState::Init;
[357](#357)        let ro_access = AccessFs::ReadDir | AccessFs::ReadFile;
[358](#358)        assert!(matches!(
[359](#359)            PathBeneath::new(PathFd::new(file).unwrap(), ro_access)
[360](#360)                .try_compat(abi, CompatLevel::HardRequirement, &mut compat_state)
[361](#361)                .unwrap_err(),
[362](#362)            CompatError::PathBeneath(PathBeneathError::DirectoryAccess { access, incompatible })
[363](#363)                if access == ro_access && incompatible == AccessFs::ReadDir
[364](#364)        ));
[365](#365)
[366](#366)        let mut compat_state = CompatState::Init;
[367](#367)        assert!(matches!(
[368](#368)            PathBeneath::new(PathFd::new(file).unwrap(), BitFlags::EMPTY)
[369](#369)                .try_compat(abi, CompatLevel::BestEffort, &mut compat_state)
[370](#370)                .unwrap_err(),
[371](#371)            CompatError::Access(AccessError::Empty)
[372](#372)        ));
[373](#373)    }
[374](#374)
[375](#375)    let full_access = AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V1);
[376](#376)    for compat_level in &[
[377](#377)        CompatLevel::BestEffort,
[378](#378)        CompatLevel::SoftRequirement,
[379](#379)        CompatLevel::HardRequirement,
[380](#380)    ] {
[381](#381)        let mut compat_state = CompatState::Init;
[382](#382)        let mut path_beneath = PathBeneath::new(PathFd::new("/").unwrap(), full_access)
[383](#383)            .try_compat(abi, *compat_level, &mut compat_state)
[384](#384)            .unwrap()
[385](#385)            .unwrap();
[386](#386)        assert_eq!(compat_state, CompatState::Full);
[387](#387)
[388](#388)        let raw_access = path_beneath.attr.allowed_access;
[390](#390)        assert_eq!(raw_access, 0);
[391](#391)
[392](#392)        let _ = path_beneath.as_ptr();
[394](#394)        let raw_access = path_beneath.attr.allowed_access;
[395](#395)        assert_eq!(raw_access, full_access.bits());
[396](#396)    }

[553](#553)pub fn path_beneath_rules<I, P, A>(
[597](#597)    paths: I,
[598](#598)    access: A,
[599](#599)) -> impl Iterator<Item = Result<PathBeneath<PathFd>, RulesetError>>
[600](#600)where
[601](#601)    I: IntoIterator<Item = P>,
[602](#602)    P: AsRef<Path>,
[603](#603)    A: Into<BitFlags<AccessFs>>,
[604](#604){
[605](#605)    let access = access.into();
[606](#606)    paths.into_iter().filter_map(move |p| match PathFd::new(p) {
[607](#607)        Ok(f) => {
[608](#608)            let valid_access = match is_file(&f) {
[609](#609)                Ok(true) => access & ACCESS_FILE,
[610](#610)                Err(_) | Ok(false) => access,
[612](#612)            };
[613](#613)            Some(Ok(PathBeneath::new(f, valid_access)))
[614](#614)        }
[615](#615)        Err(_) => None,
[616](#616)    })
[617](#617)}

[236](#236)impl Ruleset {

[239](#239)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[240](#240)        Ruleset::default()
[241](#241)    }
[242](#242)
[243](#243)    pub fn create(mut self) -> Result<RulesetCreated, RulesetError> {
[248](#248)        let body = || -> Result<RulesetCreated, CreateRulesetError> {
[249](#249)            match self.compat.state {
[250](#250)                CompatState::Init => {
[251](#251)                    Err(CreateRulesetError::MissingHandledAccess)
[254](#254)                }
[255](#255)                CompatState::No | CompatState::Dummy => {
[256](#256)                    #[cfg(test)]
[258](#258)                    assert!(
[259](#259)                        !self.requested_handled_fs.is_empty()
[260](#260)                            || !self.requested_handled_net.is_empty()
[261](#261)                            || !self.requested_scoped.is_empty()
[262](#262)                    );
[263](#263)
[264](#264)                    self.compat.update(CompatState::Dummy);
[267](#267)                    match self.compat.level.into() {
[268](#268)                        CompatLevel::HardRequirement => {
[269](#269)                            Err(CreateRulesetError::MissingHandledAccess)
[270](#270)                        }
[271](#271)                        _ => Ok(RulesetCreated::new(self, None)),
[272](#272)                    }
[273](#273)                }
[274](#274)                CompatState::Full | CompatState::Partial => {
[275](#275)                    #[cfg(test)]
[277](#277)                    assert!(
[278](#278)                        !self.actual_handled_fs.is_empty()
[279](#279)                            || !self.actual_handled_net.is_empty()
[280](#280)                            || !self.actual_scoped.is_empty()
[281](#281)                    );
[282](#282)
[283](#283)                    let attr = uapi::landlock_ruleset_attr {
[284](#284)                        handled_access_fs: self.actual_handled_fs.bits(),
[285](#285)                        handled_access_net: self.actual_handled_net.bits(),
[286](#286)                        scoped: self.actual_scoped.bits(),
[287](#287)                    };
[288](#288)                    match unsafe { uapi::landlock_create_ruleset(&attr, size_of_val(&attr), 0) } {
[289](#289)                        fd if fd >= 0 => Ok(RulesetCreated::new(
[290](#290)                            self,
[291](#291)                            Some(unsafe { OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd) }),
[292](#292)                        )),
[293](#293)                        _ => Err(CreateRulesetError::CreateRulesetCall {
[294](#294)                            source: Error::last_os_error(),
[295](#295)                        }),
[296](#296)                    }
[297](#297)                }
[298](#298)            }
[299](#299)        };
[300](#300)        Ok(body()?)
[301](#301)    }
[302](#302)}

[340](#340)pub trait RulesetAttr: Sized + AsMut<Ruleset> + Compatible {
[341](#341)    fn handle_access<T, U>(mut self, access: T) -> Result<Self, RulesetError>
[349](#349)    where
[350](#350)        T: Into<BitFlags<U>>,
[351](#351)        U: HandledAccess + PrivateHandledAccess,
[352](#352)    {
[353](#353)        U::ruleset_handle_access(self.as_mut(), access.into())?;
[354](#354)        Ok(self)
[355](#355)    }
[356](#356)
[357](#357)    fn scope<T>(mut self, scope: T) -> Result<Self, RulesetError>
[364](#364)    where
[365](#365)        T: Into<BitFlags<Scope>>,
[366](#366)    {
[367](#367)        let scope = scope.into();
[368](#368)        let ruleset = self.as_mut();
[369](#369)        ruleset.requested_scoped |= scope;
[370](#370)        if let Some(a) = scope
[371](#371)            .try_compat(
[372](#372)                ruleset.compat.abi(),
[373](#373)                ruleset.compat.level,
[374](#374)                &mut ruleset.compat.state,
[375](#375)            )
[376](#376)            .map_err(ScopeError::Compat)?
[377](#377)        {
[378](#378)            ruleset.actual_scoped |= a;
[379](#379)        }
[380](#380)        Ok(self)
[381](#381)    }
[382](#382)}

[659](#659)impl RestrictSelfFlagsState for RulesetCreated {
[660](#660)    fn try_set_flag(&mut self, flag: RestrictSelfFlag, set: bool) -> Result<(), RulesetError> {
[661](#661)        let raw_bit = flag.raw_bit();
[662](#662)        if set == flag.default_value() {
[672](#672)            self.requested_restrict_self_flags &= !raw_bit;
[673](#673)        } else {
[674](#674)            self.requested_restrict_self_flags |= raw_bit;
[675](#675)        }
[676](#676)        if flag.try_compat(set, &mut self.compat)? {
[677](#677)            self.actual_restrict_self_flags |= raw_bit;
[678](#678)        } else {
[679](#679)            self.actual_restrict_self_flags &= !raw_bit;
[680](#680)        }
[681](#681)        Ok(())
[682](#682)    }
[683](#683)}
[684](#684)
[685](#685)impl RestrictSelfFlagsState for &mut RulesetCreated {
[686](#686)    fn try_set_flag(&mut self, flag: RestrictSelfFlag, set: bool) -> Result<(), RulesetError> {
[687](#687)        (**self).try_set_flag(flag, set)
[688](#688)    }

[693](#693)
[694](#694)pub trait RulesetCreatedAttr:
[695](#695)    Sized + AsMut<RulesetCreated> + Compatible + RestrictSelfAttr
[696](#696){
[697](#697)    fn add_rule<T, U>(mut self, rule: T) -> Result<Self, RulesetError>
[701](#701)    where
[702](#702)        T: Rule<U>,
[703](#703)        U: HandledAccess + PrivateHandledAccess,
[704](#704)    {
[705](#705)        let body = || -> Result<Self, AddRulesError> {
[706](#706)            let self_ref = self.as_mut();
[707](#707)            rule.check_consistency(self_ref)?;
[708](#708)            let mut compat_rule = match rule
[709](#709)                .try_compat(
[710](#710)                    self_ref.compat.abi(),
[711](#711)                    self_ref.compat.level,
[712](#712)                    &mut self_ref.compat.state,
[713](#713)                )
[714](#714)                .map_err(AddRuleError::Compat)?
[715](#715)            {
[716](#716)                Some(r) => r,
[717](#717)                None => return Ok(self),
[718](#718)            };
[719](#719)            match self_ref.compat.state {
[720](#720)                CompatState::Init | CompatState::No | CompatState::Dummy => Ok(self),
[721](#721)                CompatState::Full | CompatState::Partial => {
[722](#722)                    #[cfg(test)]
[723](#723)                    assert!(self_ref.fd.is_some());
[724](#724)                    let fd = self_ref.fd.as_ref().map(|f| f.as_raw_fd()).unwrap_or(-1);
[725](#725)                    match unsafe {
[726](#726)                        uapi::landlock_add_rule(fd, T::TYPE_ID, compat_rule.as_ptr(), 0)
[727](#727)                    } {
[728](#728)                        0 => Ok(self),
[729](#729)                        _ => Err(AddRuleError::<U>::AddRuleCall {
[730](#730)                            source: Error::last_os_error(),
[731](#731)                        }
[732](#732)                        .into()),
[733](#733)                    }
[734](#734)                }
[735](#735)            }
[736](#736)        };
[737](#737)        Ok(body()?)
[738](#738)    }
[739](#739)
[740](#740)    fn add_rules<I, T, U, E>(mut self, rules: I) -> Result<Self, E>
[815](#815)    where
[816](#816)        I: IntoIterator<Item = Result<T, E>>,
[817](#817)        T: Rule<U>,
[818](#818)        U: HandledAccess + PrivateHandledAccess,
[819](#819)        E: From<RulesetError>,
[820](#820)    {
[821](#821)        for rule in rules {
[822](#822)            self = self.add_rule(rule?)?;
[823](#823)        }
[824](#824)        Ok(self)
[825](#825)    }
[826](#826)
[827](#827)    fn no_new_privs(mut self, yes: bool) -> Self {
[833](#833)        <Self as AsMut<RulesetCreated>>::as_mut(&mut self).no_new_privs = yes;
[834](#834)        self
[835](#835)    }
[836](#836)
[837](#837)    #[deprecated(note = "Use no_new_privs() instead.")]
[839](#839)    fn set_no_new_privs(self, yes: bool) -> Self {
[840](#840)        self.no_new_privs(yes)
[841](#841)    }
[842](#842)
[843](#843)    fn log_same_exec(mut self, set: bool) -> Result<Self, RulesetError> {
[856](#856)        self.try_set_flag(RestrictSelfFlag::LogSameExec, set)?;
[857](#857)        Ok(self)
[858](#858)    }
[859](#859)
[860](#860)    fn log_new_exec(mut self, set: bool) -> Result<Self, RulesetError> {
[872](#872)        self.try_set_flag(RestrictSelfFlag::LogNewExec, set)?;
[873](#873)        Ok(self)
[874](#874)    }
[875](#875)}
[876](#876)
[877](#877)#[derive(Debug)]
[879](#879)pub struct RulesetCreated {
[880](#880)    fd: Option<OwnedFd>,
[881](#881)    no_new_privs: bool,
[882](#882)    pub(crate) requested_handled_fs: BitFlags<AccessFs>,
[883](#883)    pub(crate) requested_handled_net: BitFlags<AccessNet>,
[884](#884)    requested_restrict_self_flags: u32,
[885](#885)    actual_restrict_self_flags: u32,
[886](#886)    compat: Compatibility,
[887](#887)}
[888](#888)
[889](#889)impl RulesetCreated {
[890](#890)    pub(crate) fn new(ruleset: Ruleset, fd: Option<OwnedFd>) -> Self {
[891](#891)        #[cfg(test)]
[893](#893)        assert!(!matches!(ruleset.compat.state, CompatState::Init));
[894](#894)
[895](#895)        RulesetCreated {
[896](#896)            fd,
[897](#897)            no_new_privs: true,
[898](#898)            requested_handled_fs: ruleset.requested_handled_fs,
[899](#899)            requested_handled_net: ruleset.requested_handled_net,
[900](#900)            requested_restrict_self_flags: 0,
[901](#901)            actual_restrict_self_flags: 0,
[902](#902)            compat: ruleset.compat,
[903](#903)        }
[904](#904)    }
[905](#905)
[906](#906)    pub fn restrict_self(mut self) -> Result<RestrictionStatus, RulesetError> {
[914](#914)        let mut body = || -> Result<RestrictionStatus, RestrictSelfError> {
[915](#915)            let enforced_nnp = if self.no_new_privs {
[919](#919)                try_set_no_new_privs(&mut self.compat)?
[920](#920)            } else {
[921](#921)                false
[922](#922)            };
[923](#923)
[924](#924)            let raw = self.actual_restrict_self_flags;
[925](#925)            let log_same_exec = RestrictSelfFlag::LogSameExec.is_set(raw);
[926](#926)            let log_new_exec = RestrictSelfFlag::LogNewExec.is_set(raw);
[927](#927)            let log_subdomains = RestrictSelfFlag::LogSubdomains.is_set(raw);
[928](#928)
[929](#929)            match self.compat.state {
[930](#930)                CompatState::Init | CompatState::No | CompatState::Dummy => Ok(RestrictionStatus {
[931](#931)                    ruleset: self.compat.state.into(),
[932](#932)                    landlock: self.compat.status(),
[933](#933)                    no_new_privs: enforced_nnp,
[934](#934)                    log_same_exec,
[935](#935)                    log_new_exec,
[936](#936)                    log_subdomains,
[937](#937)                }),
[938](#938)                CompatState::Full | CompatState::Partial => {
[939](#939)                    #[cfg(test)]
[940](#940)                    assert!(self.fd.is_some());
[941](#941)                    let fd = self.fd.as_ref().map(|f| f.as_raw_fd()).unwrap_or(-1);
[943](#943)                    match unsafe {
[944](#944)                        uapi::landlock_restrict_self(fd, self.actual_restrict_self_flags)
[945](#945)                    } {
[946](#946)                        0 => {
[947](#947)                            self.compat.update(CompatState::Full);
[948](#948)                            Ok(RestrictionStatus {
[949](#949)                                ruleset: self.compat.state.into(),
[950](#950)                                landlock: self.compat.status(),
[951](#951)                                no_new_privs: enforced_nnp,
[952](#952)                                log_same_exec,
[953](#953)                                log_new_exec,
[954](#954)                                log_subdomains,
[955](#955)                            })
[956](#956)                        }
[957](#957)                        _ => Err(RestrictSelfError::RestrictSelfCall {
[959](#959)                            source: Error::last_os_error(),
[960](#960)                        }),
[961](#961)                    }
[962](#962)                }
[963](#963)            }
[964](#964)        };
[965](#965)        Ok(body()?)
[966](#966)    }
[967](#967)
[968](#968)    pub fn try_clone(&self) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
[973](#973)        Ok(RulesetCreated {
[974](#974)            fd: self.fd.as_ref().map(|f| f.try_clone()).transpose()?,
[975](#975)            no_new_privs: self.no_new_privs,
[976](#976)            requested_handled_fs: self.requested_handled_fs,
[977](#977)            requested_handled_net: self.requested_handled_net,
[978](#978)            requested_restrict_self_flags: self.requested_restrict_self_flags,
[979](#979)            actual_restrict_self_flags: self.actual_restrict_self_flags,
[980](#980)            compat: self.compat,
[981](#981)        })
[982](#982)    }
[983](#983)}
[984](#984)

[987](#987)        ruleset.fd

[1093](#1093)            ))

# compat.rs - source

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/src/landlock/compat.rs.html

# landlock/compat.rs

[1](https://landlock.io#1)// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR MIT
[2](https://landlock.io#2)
[3](https://landlock.io#3)use crate::{uapi, Access, CompatError};
[4](https://landlock.io#4)use std::fmt::{self, Display, Formatter};
[5](https://landlock.io#5)use std::io::Error;
[6](https://landlock.io#6)
[7](https://landlock.io#7)#[cfg(test)]
[8](https://landlock.io#8)use std::convert::TryInto;
[9](https://landlock.io#9)#[cfg(test)]
[10](https://landlock.io#10)use strum::{EnumCount, IntoEnumIterator};
[11](https://landlock.io#11)#[cfg(test)]
[12](https://landlock.io#12)use strum_macros::{EnumCount as EnumCountMacro, EnumIter};
[13](https://landlock.io#13)
[14](https://landlock.io#14)/// Version of the Landlock [ABI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_binary_interface).
[15](https://landlock.io#15)///
[16](https://landlock.io#16)/// `ABI` enables getting the features supported by a specific Landlock ABI
[17](https://landlock.io#17)/// (without relying on the kernel version which may not be accessible or patched).
[18](https://landlock.io#18)/// For example, [`AccessFs::from_all(ABI::V1)`](Access::from_all)
[19](https://landlock.io#19)/// gets all the file system access rights defined by the first version.
[20](https://landlock.io#20)///
[21](https://landlock.io#21)/// Without `ABI`, it would be hazardous to rely on the the full set of access flags
[22](https://landlock.io#22)/// (e.g., `BitFlags::<AccessFs>::all()` or `BitFlags::ALL`),
[23](https://landlock.io#23)/// a moving target that would change the semantics of your Landlock rule
[24](https://landlock.io#24)/// when migrating to a newer version of this crate.
[25](https://landlock.io#25)/// Indeed, a simple `cargo update` or `cargo install` run by any developer
[26](https://landlock.io#26)/// can result in a new version of this crate (fixing bugs or bringing non-breaking changes).
[27](https://landlock.io#27)/// This crate cannot give any guarantee concerning the new restrictions resulting from
[28](https://landlock.io#28)/// these unknown bits (i.e. access rights) that would not be controlled by your application but by
[29](https://landlock.io#29)/// a future version of this crate instead.
[30](https://landlock.io#30)/// Because we cannot know what the effect on your application of an unknown restriction would be
[31](https://landlock.io#31)/// when handling an untested Landlock access right (i.e. denied-by-default access),
[32](https://landlock.io#32)/// it could trigger bugs in your application.
[33](https://landlock.io#33)///
[34](https://landlock.io#34)/// This crate provides a set of tools to sandbox as much as possible
[35](https://landlock.io#35)/// while guaranteeing a consistent behavior thanks to the [`Compatible`] methods.
[36](https://landlock.io#36)/// You should also test with different relevant kernel versions,
[37](https://landlock.io#37)/// see [landlock-test-tools](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/landlock-test-tools) and
[38](https://landlock.io#38)/// [CI integration](https://github.com/landlock-lsm/rust-landlock/pull/41).
[39](https://landlock.io#39)///
[40](https://landlock.io#40)/// This way, we can have the guarantee that the use of a set of tested Landlock ABI works as
[41](https://landlock.io#41)/// expected because features brought by newer Landlock ABI will never be enabled by default
[42](https://landlock.io#42)/// (cf. [Linux kernel compatibility contract](https://docs.kernel.org/userspace-api/landlock.html#compatibility)).
[43](https://landlock.io#43)///
[44](https://landlock.io#44)/// In a nutshell, test the access rights you request on a kernel that support them and
[45](https://landlock.io#45)/// on a kernel that doesn't support them.
[46](https://landlock.io#46)///
[47](https://landlock.io#47)/// Derived `Debug` formats are [not stable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/fmt/trait.Debug.html#stability).
[48](https://landlock.io#48)#[cfg_attr(test, derive(EnumIter, EnumCountMacro))]
[49](https://landlock.io#49)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
[50](https://landlock.io#50)#[non_exhaustive]
[51](https://landlock.io#51)pub enum ABI {
[52](https://landlock.io#52)    /// Kernel not supporting Landlock, either because it is not built with Landlock
[53](https://landlock.io#53)    /// or Landlock is not enabled at boot.
[54](https://landlock.io#54)    Unsupported = 0,
[55](https://landlock.io#55)    /// First Landlock ABI, introduced with
[56](https://landlock.io#56)    /// [Linux 5.13](https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/17ae69aba89dbfa2139b7f8024b757ab3cc42f59).
[57](https://landlock.io#57)    V1 = 1,
[58](https://landlock.io#58)    /// Second Landlock ABI, introduced with
[59](https://landlock.io#59)    /// [Linux 5.19](https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/cb44e4f061e16be65b8a16505e121490c66d30d0).
[60](https://landlock.io#60)    V2 = 2,
[61](https://landlock.io#61)    /// Third Landlock ABI, introduced with
[62](https://landlock.io#62)    /// [Linux 6.2](https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/299e2b1967578b1442128ba8b3e86ed3427d3651).
[63](https://landlock.io#63)    V3 = 3,
[64](https://landlock.io#64)    /// Fourth Landlock ABI, introduced with
[65](https://landlock.io#65)    /// [Linux 6.7](https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/136cc1e1f5be75f57f1e0404b94ee1c8792cb07d).
[66](https://landlock.io#66)    V4 = 4,
[67](https://landlock.io#67)    /// Fifth Landlock ABI, introduced with
[68](https://landlock.io#68)    /// [Linux 6.10](https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/2fc0e7892c10734c1b7c613ef04836d57d4676d5).
[69](https://landlock.io#69)    V5 = 5,
[70](https://landlock.io#70)    /// Sixth Landlock ABI, introduced with
[71](https://landlock.io#71)    /// [Linux 6.12](https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/e1b061b444fb01c237838f0d8238653afe6a8094).
[72](https://landlock.io#72)    V6 = 6,
[73](https://landlock.io#73)    /// Seventh Landlock ABI, introduced with
[74](https://landlock.io#74)    /// [Linux 6.15](https://git.kernel.org/stable/c/72885116069abdd05c245707c3989fc605632970).
[75](https://landlock.io#75)    V7 = 7,
[76](https://landlock.io#76)}
[77](https://landlock.io#77)
[78](https://landlock.io#78)// ABI should not be dynamically created (in other crates) according to the running kernel
[79](https://landlock.io#79)// to avoid inconsistent behaviors and non-determinism. Creating ABIs based on runtime detection
[80](https://landlock.io#80)// can lead to unreliable sandboxing where rules might differ between executions.
[81](https://landlock.io#81)impl ABI {
[82](https://landlock.io#82)    #[cfg(test)]
[83](https://landlock.io#83)    fn is_known(value: i32) -> bool {
[84](https://landlock.io#84)        value > 0 && value < ABI::COUNT as i32
[85](https://landlock.io#85)    }
[86](https://landlock.io#86)}
[87](https://landlock.io#87)
[88](https://landlock.io#88)/// Converting from an integer to an ABI should only be used for testing.
[89](https://landlock.io#89)/// Indeed, manually setting the ABI can lead to inconsistent and unexpected behaviors.
[90](https://landlock.io#90)/// Instead, just use the appropriate access rights, this library will handle the rest.
[91](https://landlock.io#91)impl From<i32> for ABI {
[92](https://landlock.io#92)    fn from(value: i32) -> ABI {
[93](https://landlock.io#93)        match value {
[94](https://landlock.io#94)            n if n <= 0 => ABI::Unsupported,
[95](https://landlock.io#95)            1 => ABI::V1,
[96](https://landlock.io#96)            2 => ABI::V2,
[97](https://landlock.io#97)            3 => ABI::V3,
[98](https://landlock.io#98)            4 => ABI::V4,
[99](https://landlock.io#99)            5 => ABI::V5,
[100](https://landlock.io#100)            6 => ABI::V6,
[101](https://landlock.io#101)            // Returns the greatest known ABI.
[102](https://landlock.io#102)            _ => ABI::V7,
[103](https://landlock.io#103)        }
[104](https://landlock.io#104)    }
[105](https://landlock.io#105)}
[106](https://landlock.io#106)
[107](https://landlock.io#107)#[test]
[108](https://landlock.io#108)fn abi_from() {
[109](https://landlock.io#109)    // EOPNOTSUPP (-95), ENOSYS (-38)
[110](https://landlock.io#110)    for n in [-95, -38, -1, 0] {
[111](https://landlock.io#111)        assert_eq!(ABI::from(n), ABI::Unsupported);
[112](https://landlock.io#112)    }
[113](https://landlock.io#113)
[114](https://landlock.io#114)    let mut last_i = 1;
[115](https://landlock.io#115)    let mut last_abi = ABI::Unsupported;
[116](https://landlock.io#116)    for (i, abi) in ABI::iter().enumerate() {
[117](https://landlock.io#117)        last_i = i.try_into().unwrap();
[118](https://landlock.io#118)        last_abi = abi;
[119](https://landlock.io#119)        assert_eq!(ABI::from(last_i), last_abi);
[120](https://landlock.io#120)    }
[121](https://landlock.io#121)
[122](https://landlock.io#122)    assert_eq!(ABI::from(last_i + 1), last_abi);
[123](https://landlock.io#123)    assert_eq!(ABI::from(999), last_abi);
[124](https://landlock.io#124)}
[125](https://landlock.io#125)
[126](https://landlock.io#126)#[test]
[127](https://landlock.io#127)fn known_abi() {
[128](https://landlock.io#128)    assert!(!ABI::is_known(-1));
[129](https://landlock.io#129)    assert!(!ABI::is_known(0));
[130](https://landlock.io#130)    assert!(!ABI::is_known(999));
[131](https://landlock.io#131)
[132](https://landlock.io#132)    let mut last_i = -1;
[133](https://landlock.io#133)    for (i, _) in ABI::iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
[134](https://landlock.io#134)        last_i = i as i32;
[135](https://landlock.io#135)        assert!(ABI::is_known(last_i));
[136](https://landlock.io#136)    }
[137](https://landlock.io#137)    assert!(!ABI::is_known(last_i + 1));
[138](https://landlock.io#138)}
[139](https://landlock.io#139)
[140](https://landlock.io#140)impl Display for ABI {
[141](https://landlock.io#141)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[142](https://landlock.io#142)        match self {
[143](https://landlock.io#143)            ABI::Unsupported => write!(f, "unsupported"),
[144](https://landlock.io#144)            v => (*v as u32).fmt(f),
[145](https://landlock.io#145)        }
[146](https://landlock.io#146)    }
[147](https://landlock.io#147)}
[148](https://landlock.io#148)
[149](https://landlock.io#149)/// Status of Landlock support for the running system.
[150](https://landlock.io#150)///
[151](https://landlock.io#151)/// This enum is used to represent the status of the Landlock support for the system where the code
[152](https://landlock.io#152)/// is executed. It can indicate whether Landlock is available or not.
[153](https://landlock.io#153)///
[154](https://landlock.io#154)/// # Warning
[155](https://landlock.io#155)///
[156](https://landlock.io#156)/// Sandboxed programs should only use this data to log or provide information to users,
[157](https://landlock.io#157)/// not to change their behavior according to this status.  Indeed, the `Ruleset` and the other
[158](https://landlock.io#158)/// types are designed to handle the compatibility in a simple and safe way.
[159](https://landlock.io#159)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[160](https://landlock.io#160)pub enum LandlockStatus {
[161](https://landlock.io#161)    /// Landlock is supported but not enabled (`EOPNOTSUPP`).
[162](https://landlock.io#162)    NotEnabled,
[163](https://landlock.io#163)    /// Landlock is not implemented (i.e. not built into the running kernel: `ENOSYS`).
[164](https://landlock.io#164)    NotImplemented,
[165](https://landlock.io#165)    /// Landlock is available and working on the running system.
[166](https://landlock.io#166)    ///
[167](https://landlock.io#167)    /// This indicates that the kernel supports Landlock and it's properly enabled.
[168](https://landlock.io#168)    /// The crate uses the `effective_abi` for all operations, which represents
[169](https://landlock.io#169)    /// the highest ABI version that both the kernel and this crate understand.
[170](https://landlock.io#170)    Available {
[171](https://landlock.io#171)        /// The effective ABI version that this crate will use for Landlock operations.
[172](https://landlock.io#172)        /// This is the intersection of what the kernel supports and what this crate knows about.
[173](https://landlock.io#173)        effective_abi: ABI,
[174](https://landlock.io#174)        /// The actual kernel ABI version when it's newer than any ABI supported by this crate.
[175](https://landlock.io#175)        ///
[176](https://landlock.io#176)        /// If `Some(version)`, it means the running kernel supports Landlock ABI `version`
[177](https://landlock.io#177)        /// which is higher than the latest ABI known by this crate.
[178](https://landlock.io#178)        ///
[179](https://landlock.io#179)        /// This field is purely informational and is never used for Landlock operations.
[180](https://landlock.io#180)        /// The crate always and only uses `effective_abi` for all functionality.
[181](https://landlock.io#181)        kernel_abi: Option<i32>,
[182](https://landlock.io#182)    },
[183](https://landlock.io#183)}
[184](https://landlock.io#184)
[185](https://landlock.io#185)impl LandlockStatus {
[186](https://landlock.io#186)    // Must remain private to avoid inconsistent behavior using such unknown-at-build-time ABI
[187](https://landlock.io#187)    // e.g., AccessFs::from_all(ABI::new_current())
[188](https://landlock.io#188)    //
[189](https://landlock.io#189)    // This should not be Default::default() because the returned value would may not be the same
[190](https://landlock.io#190)    // for all users.
[191](https://landlock.io#191)    fn current() -> Self {
[192](https://landlock.io#192)        // Landlock ABI version starts at 1 but errno is only set for negative values.
[193](https://landlock.io#193)        let v = unsafe {
[194](https://landlock.io#194)            uapi::landlock_create_ruleset(
[195](https://landlock.io#195)                std::ptr::null(),
[196](https://landlock.io#196)                0,
[197](https://landlock.io#197)                uapi::LANDLOCK_CREATE_RULESET_VERSION,
[198](https://landlock.io#198)            )
[199](https://landlock.io#199)        };
[200](https://landlock.io#200)        if v < 0 {
[201](https://landlock.io#201)            // The only possible error values should be EOPNOTSUPP and ENOSYS.
[202](https://landlock.io#202)            match Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error() {
[203](https://landlock.io#203)                Some(libc::EOPNOTSUPP) => Self::NotEnabled,
[204](https://landlock.io#204)                _ => Self::NotImplemented,
[205](https://landlock.io#205)            }
[206](https://landlock.io#206)        } else {
[207](https://landlock.io#207)            let abi = ABI::from(v);
[208](https://landlock.io#208)            Self::Available {
[209](https://landlock.io#209)                effective_abi: abi,
[210](https://landlock.io#210)                kernel_abi: (v != abi as i32).then_some(v),
[211](https://landlock.io#211)            }
[212](https://landlock.io#212)        }
[213](https://landlock.io#213)    }
[214](https://landlock.io#214)}
[215](https://landlock.io#215)
[216](https://landlock.io#216)// Test against the running kernel.
[217](https://landlock.io#217)#[test]
[218](https://landlock.io#218)fn test_current_landlock_status() {
[219](https://landlock.io#219)    let status = LandlockStatus::current();
[220](https://landlock.io#220)    if *TEST_ABI == ABI::Unsupported {
[221](https://landlock.io#221)        assert_eq!(status, LandlockStatus::NotImplemented);
[222](https://landlock.io#222)    } else {
[223](https://landlock.io#223)        assert!(
[224](https://landlock.io#224)            matches!(status, LandlockStatus::Available { effective_abi, .. } if effective_abi == *TEST_ABI)
[225](https://landlock.io#225)        );
[226](https://landlock.io#226)        if std::env::var(TEST_ABI_ENV_NAME).is_ok() {
[227](https://landlock.io#227)            // We cannot reliably check for unknown kernel.
[228](https://landlock.io#228)            assert!(matches!(
[229](https://landlock.io#229)                status,
[230](https://landlock.io#230)                LandlockStatus::Available {
[231](https://landlock.io#231)                    kernel_abi: None,
[232](https://landlock.io#232)                    ..
[233](https://landlock.io#233)                }
[234](https://landlock.io#234)            ));
[235](https://landlock.io#235)        }
[236](https://landlock.io#236)    }
[237](https://landlock.io#237)}
[238](https://landlock.io#238)
[239](https://landlock.io#239)impl From<LandlockStatus> for ABI {
[240](https://landlock.io#240)    fn from(status: LandlockStatus) -> Self {
[241](https://landlock.io#241)        match status {
[242](https://landlock.io#242)            // The only possible error values should be EOPNOTSUPP and ENOSYS,
[243](https://landlock.io#243)            // but let's convert all kind of errors as unsupported.
[244](https://landlock.io#244)            LandlockStatus::NotEnabled | LandlockStatus::NotImplemented => ABI::Unsupported,
[245](https://landlock.io#245)            LandlockStatus::Available { effective_abi, .. } => effective_abi,
[246](https://landlock.io#246)        }
[247](https://landlock.io#247)    }
[248](https://landlock.io#248)}
[249](https://landlock.io#249)
[250](https://landlock.io#250)// This is only useful to tests and should not be exposed publicly because
[251](https://landlock.io#251)// the mapping can only be partial.
[252](https://landlock.io#252)#[cfg(test)]
[253](https://landlock.io#253)impl From<ABI> for LandlockStatus {
[254](https://landlock.io#254)    fn from(abi: ABI) -> Self {
[255](https://landlock.io#255)        match abi {
[256](https://landlock.io#256)            // Convert to ENOSYS because of check_ruleset_support() and ruleset_unsupported() tests.
[257](https://landlock.io#257)            ABI::Unsupported => Self::NotImplemented,
[258](https://landlock.io#258)            _ => Self::Available {
[259](https://landlock.io#259)                effective_abi: abi,
[260](https://landlock.io#260)                kernel_abi: None,
[261](https://landlock.io#261)            },
[262](https://landlock.io#262)        }
[263](https://landlock.io#263)    }
[264](https://landlock.io#264)}
[265](https://landlock.io#265)
[266](https://landlock.io#266)#[cfg(test)]
[267](https://landlock.io#267)pub(crate) static TEST_ABI_ENV_NAME: &str = "LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI";
[268](https://landlock.io#268)
[269](https://landlock.io#269)#[cfg(test)]
[270](https://landlock.io#270)lazy_static! {
[271](https://landlock.io#271)    pub(crate) static ref TEST_ABI: ABI = match std::env::var("LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI") {
[272](https://landlock.io#272)        Ok(s) => {
[273](https://landlock.io#273)            let n = s.parse::<i32>().unwrap();
[274](https://landlock.io#274)            if ABI::is_known(n) || n == 0 {
[275](https://landlock.io#275)                ABI::from(n)
[276](https://landlock.io#276)            } else {
[277](https://landlock.io#277)                panic!("Unknown ABI: {n}");
[278](https://landlock.io#278)            }
[279](https://landlock.io#279)        }
[280](https://landlock.io#280)        Err(std::env::VarError::NotPresent) => LandlockStatus::current().into(),
[281](https://landlock.io#281)        Err(e) => panic!("Failed to read LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI: {e}"),
[282](https://landlock.io#282)    };
[283](https://landlock.io#283)}
[284](https://landlock.io#284)
[285](https://landlock.io#285)#[cfg(test)]
[286](https://landlock.io#286)pub(crate) fn can_emulate(mock: ABI, partial_support: ABI, full_support: Option<ABI>) -> bool {
[287](https://landlock.io#287)    mock < partial_support
[288](https://landlock.io#288)        || mock <= *TEST_ABI
[289](https://landlock.io#289)        || if let Some(full) = full_support {
[290](https://landlock.io#290)            full <= *TEST_ABI
[291](https://landlock.io#291)        } else {
[292](https://landlock.io#292)            partial_support <= *TEST_ABI
[293](https://landlock.io#293)        }
[294](https://landlock.io#294)}
[295](https://landlock.io#295)
[296](https://landlock.io#296)#[cfg(test)]
[297](https://landlock.io#297)pub(crate) fn get_errno_from_landlock_status() -> Option<i32> {
[298](https://landlock.io#298)    match LandlockStatus::current() {
[299](https://landlock.io#299)        LandlockStatus::NotImplemented | LandlockStatus::NotEnabled => {
[300](https://landlock.io#300)            match Error::last_os_error().raw_os_error() {
[301](https://landlock.io#301)                // Returns ENOSYS when the kernel is not built with Landlock support,
[302](https://landlock.io#302)                // or EOPNOTSUPP when Landlock is supported but disabled at boot time.
[303](https://landlock.io#303)                ret @ Some(libc::ENOSYS | libc::EOPNOTSUPP) => ret,
[304](https://landlock.io#304)                // Other values can only come from bogus seccomp filters or debugging tampering.
[305](https://landlock.io#305)                ret => {
[306](https://landlock.io#306)                    eprintln!("Current kernel should support this Landlock ABI according to $LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI");
[307](https://landlock.io#307)                    eprintln!("Unexpected result: {ret:?}");
[308](https://landlock.io#308)                    unreachable!();
[309](https://landlock.io#309)                }
[310](https://landlock.io#310)            }
[311](https://landlock.io#311)        }
[312](https://landlock.io#312)        LandlockStatus::Available { .. } => None,
[313](https://landlock.io#313)    }
[314](https://landlock.io#314)}
[315](https://landlock.io#315)
[316](https://landlock.io#316)#[test]
[317](https://landlock.io#317)fn current_kernel_abi() {
[318](https://landlock.io#318)    // Ensures that the tested Landlock ABI is the latest known version supported by the running
[319](https://landlock.io#319)    // kernel.  If this test failed, you need set the LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI environment variable
[320](https://landlock.io#320)    // to the Landlock ABI version supported by your kernel.  With a missing variable, the latest
[321](https://landlock.io#321)    // Landlock ABI version known by this crate is automatically set.
[322](https://landlock.io#322)    // From Linux 5.13 to 5.18, you need to run: LANDLOCK_CRATE_TEST_ABI=1 cargo test
[323](https://landlock.io#323)    let test_abi = *TEST_ABI;
[324](https://landlock.io#324)    let current_abi = LandlockStatus::current().into();
[325](https://landlock.io#325)    println!(
[326](https://landlock.io#326)        "Current kernel version: {}",
[327](https://landlock.io#327)        std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/version")
[328](https://landlock.io#328)            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "unknown".into())
[329](https://landlock.io#329)            .trim()
[330](https://landlock.io#330)    );
[331](https://landlock.io#331)    println!("Expected Landlock ABI {test_abi:?} whereas the current ABI is {current_abi:#?}");
[332](https://landlock.io#332)    assert_eq!(test_abi, current_abi);
[333](https://landlock.io#333)}
[334](https://landlock.io#334)
[335](https://landlock.io#335)// CompatState is not public outside this crate.
[336](https://landlock.io#336)/// Returned by ruleset builder.
[337](https://landlock.io#337)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[338](https://landlock.io#338)pub enum CompatState {
[339](https://landlock.io#339)    /// Initial undefined state.
[340](https://landlock.io#340)    Init,
[341](https://landlock.io#341)    /// All requested restrictions are enforced.
[342](https://landlock.io#342)    Full,
[343](https://landlock.io#343)    /// Some requested restrictions are enforced, following a best-effort approach.
[344](https://landlock.io#344)    Partial,
[345](https://landlock.io#345)    /// The running system doesn't support Landlock.
[346](https://landlock.io#346)    No,
[347](https://landlock.io#347)    /// Final unsupported state.
[348](https://landlock.io#348)    Dummy,
[349](https://landlock.io#349)}
[350](https://landlock.io#350)
[351](https://landlock.io#351)impl CompatState {
[352](https://landlock.io#352)    fn update(&mut self, other: Self) {
[353](https://landlock.io#353)        *self = match (*self, other) {
[354](https://landlock.io#354)            (CompatState::Init, other) => other,
[355](https://landlock.io#355)            (CompatState::Dummy, _) => CompatState::Dummy,
[356](https://landlock.io#356)            (_, CompatState::Dummy) => CompatState::Dummy,
[357](https://landlock.io#357)            (CompatState::No, CompatState::No) => CompatState::No,
[358](https://landlock.io#358)            (CompatState::Full, CompatState::Full) => CompatState::Full,
[359](https://landlock.io#359)            (_, _) => CompatState::Partial,
[360](https://landlock.io#360)        }
[361](https://landlock.io#361)    }
[362](https://landlock.io#362)}
[363](https://landlock.io#363)
[364](https://landlock.io#364)#[test]
[365](https://landlock.io#365)fn compat_state_update_1() {
[366](https://landlock.io#366)    let mut state = CompatState::Full;
[367](https://landlock.io#367)
[368](https://landlock.io#368)    state.update(CompatState::Full);
[369](https://landlock.io#369)    assert_eq!(state, CompatState::Full);
[370](https://landlock.io#370)
[371](https://landlock.io#371)    state.update(CompatState::No);
[372](https://landlock.io#372)    assert_eq!(state, CompatState::Partial);
[373](https://landlock.io#373)

[375](https://landlock.io#375)    assert_eq!(state, CompatState::Partial);
[376](https://landlock.io#376)
[377](https://landlock.io#377)    state.update(CompatState::Full);
[378](https://landlock.io#378)    assert_eq!(state, CompatState::Partial);
[379](https://landlock.io#379)
[380](https://landlock.io#380)    state.update(CompatState::No);
[381](https://landlock.io#381)    assert_eq!(state, CompatState::Partial);

[385](https://landlock.io#385)

[404](https://landlock.io#404)#[test]
[405](https://landlock.io#405)fn try_compat_binary_states() {
[406](https://landlock.io#406)    // Supported: state -> Full.
[407](https://landlock.io#407)    let mut compat: Compatibility = ABI::Unsupported.into();
[408](https://landlock.io#408)    assert_eq!(compat.state, CompatState::Init);
[409](https://landlock.io#409)    assert_eq!(compat.try_compat_binary(true, || "err"), Ok(true));
[410](https://landlock.io#410)    assert_eq!(compat.state, CompatState::Full);
[411](https://landlock.io#411)
[412](https://landlock.io#412)    // Unsupported + BestEffort: state -> Partial (Full + No).
[413](https://landlock.io#413)    assert_eq!(compat.try_compat_binary(false, || "err"), Ok(false));
[414](https://landlock.io#414)    assert_eq!(compat.state, CompatState::Partial);
[415](https://landlock.io#415)
[416](https://landlock.io#416)    // Unsupported + SoftRequirement: state -> Dummy.
[417](https://landlock.io#417)    let mut compat: Compatibility = ABI::Unsupported.into();
[418](https://landlock.io#418)    compat.level = Some(CompatLevel::SoftRequirement);
[419](https://landlock.io#419)    assert_eq!(compat.try_compat_binary(false, || "err"), Ok(false));
[420](https://landlock.io#420)    assert_eq!(compat.state, CompatState::Dummy);
[421](https://landlock.io#421)
[422](https://landlock.io#422)    // Unsupported + HardRequirement: returns error.
[423](https://landlock.io#423)    let mut compat: Compatibility = ABI::Unsupported.into();
[424](https://landlock.io#424)    compat.level = Some(CompatLevel::HardRequirement);
[425](https://landlock.io#425)    assert_eq!(compat.try_compat_binary(false, || "err"), Err("err"));
[426](https://landlock.io#426)}
