# flags.rs - source

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/src/landlock/flags.rs.html

# landlock/flags.rs

[1](https://landlock.io#1)// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR MIT
[2](https://landlock.io#2)
[3](https://landlock.io#3)//! Syscall flag types for `landlock_restrict_self()` and future syscall flags.
[4](https://landlock.io#4)//!
[5](https://landlock.io#5)//! This module provides a compatibility mechanism for individual syscall flags,
[6](https://landlock.io#6)//! parallel to but simpler than the [`Access`](crate::Access) /
[7](https://landlock.io#7)//! [`TryCompat`](crate::TryCompat) machinery.
[8](https://landlock.io#8)//!
[9](https://landlock.io#9)//! Key differences from the [`Access`](crate::Access) pattern:
[10](https://landlock.io#10)//!
[11](https://landlock.io#11)//! - Access types ([`AccessFs`](crate::AccessFs), [`AccessNet`](crate::AccessNet),
[12](https://landlock.io#12)//!   [`Scope`](crate::Scope)) operate on **sets** of rights passed as
[13](https://landlock.io#13)//!   [`BitFlags<T>`](enumflags2::BitFlags), where the compat result can be Full,
[14](https://landlock.io#14)//!   Partial, or No depending on which bits are supported.  They use the
[15](https://landlock.io#15)//!   [`TryCompat`](crate::TryCompat) trait and the full
[16](https://landlock.io#16)//!   [`AccessError`](crate::AccessError) hierarchy.
[17](https://landlock.io#17)//!
[18](https://landlock.io#18)//! - Syscall flags are set **individually** through boolean setter methods
[19](https://landlock.io#19)//!   (e.g., [`log_same_exec()`](crate::RulesetCreatedAttr::log_same_exec)), so
[20](https://landlock.io#20)//!   the compat result is binary: supported or not.  There is no Partial case,
[21](https://landlock.io#21)//!   no set-level validation, and no need for an
[22](https://landlock.io#22)//!   [`AccessError`](crate::AccessError)-like hierarchy.  The
[23](https://landlock.io#23)//!   [`try_compat()`](SyscallFlagExt::try_compat) default method on
[24](https://landlock.io#24)//!   [`SyscallFlagExt`] handles the compat dispatch directly, using
[25](https://landlock.io#25)//!   [`Compatibility::try_compat_binary()`](crate::compat::Compatibility::try_compat_binary)
[26](https://landlock.io#26)//!   factored out from the No branch of
[27](https://landlock.io#27)//!   [`TryCompat::try_compat()`](crate::TryCompat::try_compat).
[28](https://landlock.io#28)//!
[29](https://landlock.io#29)//! - Access types implement the [`Access`](crate::Access) trait (which requires
[30](https://landlock.io#30)//!   [`BitFlag`](enumflags2::BitFlag)) and are used with
[31](https://landlock.io#31)//!   [`BitFlags<T>`](enumflags2::BitFlags) throughout the builder.  Syscall
[32](https://landlock.io#32)//!   flags are plain enums (no `#[bitflags]`); the raw UAPI bitmask is built
[33](https://landlock.io#33)//!   internally by OR-ing the constants returned by
[34](https://landlock.io#34)//!   [`raw_bit()`](SyscallFlagExt::raw_bit) into a `u32`.
[35](https://landlock.io#35)
[36](https://landlock.io#36)use crate::compat::{Compatibility, ABI};
[37](https://landlock.io#37)use crate::errors::SyscallFlagError;
[38](https://landlock.io#38)use crate::private;
[39](https://landlock.io#39)use crate::uapi;
[40](https://landlock.io#40)
[41](https://landlock.io#41)/// Marker trait for syscall flag types used in compatibility checks.
[42](https://landlock.io#42)///
[43](https://landlock.io#43)/// This is the syscall-flag equivalent of the [`Access`](crate::Access) trait,
[44](https://landlock.io#44)/// but without the [`BitFlag`](enumflags2::BitFlag) requirement since syscall
[45](https://landlock.io#45)/// flags are set individually rather than as sets.
[46](https://landlock.io#46)///
[47](https://landlock.io#47)/// This trait is sealed and cannot be implemented outside of this crate.
[48](https://landlock.io#48)pub trait SyscallFlag: Copy + core::fmt::Debug + private::Sealed {}
[49](https://landlock.io#49)
[50](https://landlock.io#50)/// Internal extension providing compatibility logic for syscall flags.
[51](https://landlock.io#51)///
[52](https://landlock.io#52)/// This is the syscall-flag equivalent of [`TryCompat`](crate::TryCompat),
[53](https://landlock.io#53)/// simplified for single-flag boolean setters where the compat result is
[54](https://landlock.io#54)/// binary (supported or not) rather than Full/Partial/No.
[55](https://landlock.io#55)///
[56](https://landlock.io#56)/// Implementors provide [`default_value()`](Self::default_value),
[57](https://landlock.io#57)/// [`raw_bit()`](Self::raw_bit), and [`since()`](Self::since); the
[58](https://landlock.io#58)/// [`try_compat()`](Self::try_compat) default method handles the compat
[59](https://landlock.io#59)/// state update and level dispatch.
[60](https://landlock.io#60)pub(crate) trait SyscallFlagExt: SyscallFlag {
[61](https://landlock.io#61)    /// Returns the kernel's default state for this flag.
[62](https://landlock.io#62)    fn default_value(self) -> bool;
[63](https://landlock.io#63)
[64](https://landlock.io#64)    /// Returns the raw UAPI constant for this flag.
[65](https://landlock.io#65)    fn raw_bit(self) -> u32;
[66](https://landlock.io#66)
[67](https://landlock.io#67)    /// Returns the minimum ABI version that supports this flag.
[68](https://landlock.io#68)    fn since(self) -> ABI;
[69](https://landlock.io#69)
[70](https://landlock.io#70)    /// Checks compatibility and returns whether the non-default bit should
[71](https://landlock.io#71)    /// be applied.
[72](https://landlock.io#72)    ///
[73](https://landlock.io#73)    /// Returns `Ok(true)` if [`raw_bit()`](Self::raw_bit) should be set in
[74](https://landlock.io#74)    /// the actual flags.  Returns `Ok(false)` if the flag should be cleared
[75](https://landlock.io#75)    /// to its default state, either because `set == default_value()` or
[76](https://landlock.io#76)    /// because the kernel does not support the flag and the compat level
[77](https://landlock.io#77)    /// permits dropping it.  Returns `Err` if the flag is unsupported with
[78](https://landlock.io#78)    /// [`CompatLevel::HardRequirement`](crate::CompatLevel::HardRequirement).
[79](https://landlock.io#79)    ///
[80](https://landlock.io#80)    /// Setting to the default value never requires a compat check.
[81](https://landlock.io#81)    ///
[82](https://landlock.io#82)    /// This mirrors the compat dispatch in
[83](https://landlock.io#83)    /// [`TryCompat::try_compat()`](crate::TryCompat::try_compat) but without
[84](https://landlock.io#84)    /// the Partial case (a single flag is either fully supported or not).
[85](https://landlock.io#85)    fn try_compat(
[86](https://landlock.io#86)        self,
[87](https://landlock.io#87)        set: bool,
[88](https://landlock.io#88)        compat: &mut Compatibility,
[89](https://landlock.io#89)    ) -> Result<bool, SyscallFlagError<Self>> {
[90](https://landlock.io#90)        if set == self.default_value() {
[91](https://landlock.io#91)            // Setting to the default value is always safe; no compat check
[92](https://landlock.io#92)            // needed and the caller should clear the bit.
[93](https://landlock.io#93)            return Ok(false);
[94](https://landlock.io#94)        }
[95](https://landlock.io#95)        compat.try_compat_binary(compat.abi() >= self.since(), || {
[96](https://landlock.io#96)            SyscallFlagError::NotSupported { flag: self, set }
[97](https://landlock.io#97)        })
[98](https://landlock.io#98)    }
[99](https://landlock.io#99)}
[100](https://landlock.io#100)
[101](https://landlock.io#101)/// Identifies a configuration flag for the `landlock_restrict_self()` syscall.
[102](https://landlock.io#102)///
[103](https://landlock.io#103)/// Unlike access rights ([`AccessFs`](crate::AccessFs), [`AccessNet`](crate::AccessNet))
[104](https://landlock.io#104)/// and scopes ([`Scope`](crate::Scope)), these flags are not passed to
[105](https://landlock.io#105)/// `landlock_create_ruleset()` but to `landlock_restrict_self()`.  They control
[106](https://landlock.io#106)/// audit logging behavior rather than access restrictions.
[107](https://landlock.io#107)///
[108](https://landlock.io#108)/// Each flag is set through a dedicated boolean method on
[109](https://landlock.io#109)/// [`RulesetCreatedAttr`](crate::RulesetCreatedAttr) or
[110](https://landlock.io#110)/// [`RestrictSelfAttr`](crate::RestrictSelfAttr).  The polarity mapping
[111](https://landlock.io#111)/// (e.g., `log_same_exec(false)` maps to `LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SAME_EXEC_OFF`)
[112](https://landlock.io#112)/// is handled internally.
[113](https://landlock.io#113)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[114](https://landlock.io#114)#[non_exhaustive]
[115](https://landlock.io#115)// All variants intentionally share the "Log" prefix to match the kernel's
[116](https://landlock.io#116)// LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_* naming convention.  Future non-logging flags
[117](https://landlock.io#117)// (e.g., TSYNC) will break the shared prefix, removing the need for this allow.
[118](https://landlock.io#118)#[allow(clippy::enum_variant_names)]
[119](https://landlock.io#119)pub enum RestrictSelfFlag {
[120](https://landlock.io#120)    /// Same-exec logging (see [`RulesetCreatedAttr::log_same_exec()`](crate::RulesetCreatedAttr::log_same_exec)).
[121](https://landlock.io#121)    LogSameExec,
[122](https://landlock.io#122)    /// New-exec logging (see [`RulesetCreatedAttr::log_new_exec()`](crate::RulesetCreatedAttr::log_new_exec)).
[123](https://landlock.io#123)    LogNewExec,
[124](https://landlock.io#124)    /// Subdomain logging (see [`RestrictSelfAttr::log_subdomains()`](crate::RestrictSelfAttr::log_subdomains)).
[125](https://landlock.io#125)    LogSubdomains,
[126](https://landlock.io#126)}
[127](https://landlock.io#127)
[128](https://landlock.io#128)impl SyscallFlag for RestrictSelfFlag {}
[129](https://landlock.io#129)
[130](https://landlock.io#130)impl RestrictSelfFlag {
[131](https://landlock.io#131)    /// Returns the effective state of this flag given a raw bitmask of
[132](https://landlock.io#132)    /// applied flags.
[133](https://landlock.io#133)    pub(crate) fn is_set(self, raw_flags: u32) -> bool {
[134](https://landlock.io#134)        // Each flag's raw_bit() returns either an OFF or ON UAPI constant
[135](https://landlock.io#135)        // depending on the kernel's default for that flag.  When the bit
[136](https://landlock.io#136)        // is set in raw_flags, the kernel applies the opposite of the
[137](https://landlock.io#137)        // default; when unset, the default applies.
[138](https://landlock.io#138)        if raw_flags & self.raw_bit() != 0 {
[139](https://landlock.io#139)            !self.default_value()
[140](https://landlock.io#140)        } else {
[141](https://landlock.io#141)            self.default_value()
[142](https://landlock.io#142)        }
[143](https://landlock.io#143)    }
[144](https://landlock.io#144)}
[145](https://landlock.io#145)
[146](https://landlock.io#146)impl SyscallFlagExt for RestrictSelfFlag {
[147](https://landlock.io#147)    fn default_value(self) -> bool {
[148](https://landlock.io#148)        match self {
[149](https://landlock.io#149)            // Same-exec logging is enabled by default.
[150](https://landlock.io#150)            Self::LogSameExec => true,
[151](https://landlock.io#151)            // New-exec logging is disabled by default.
[152](https://landlock.io#152)            Self::LogNewExec => false,
[153](https://landlock.io#153)            // Subdomain logging is enabled by default.
[154](https://landlock.io#154)            Self::LogSubdomains => true,
[155](https://landlock.io#155)        }
[156](https://landlock.io#156)    }
[157](https://landlock.io#157)
[158](https://landlock.io#158)    fn raw_bit(self) -> u32 {
[159](https://landlock.io#159)        match self {
[160](https://landlock.io#160)            Self::LogSameExec => uapi::LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SAME_EXEC_OFF,
[161](https://landlock.io#161)            Self::LogNewExec => uapi::LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_NEW_EXEC_ON,
[162](https://landlock.io#162)            Self::LogSubdomains => uapi::LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SUBDOMAINS_OFF,
[163](https://landlock.io#163)        }
[164](https://landlock.io#164)    }
[165](https://landlock.io#165)
[166](https://landlock.io#166)    fn since(self) -> ABI {
[167](https://landlock.io#167)        match self {
[168](https://landlock.io#168)            Self::LogSameExec => ABI::V7,
[169](https://landlock.io#169)            Self::LogNewExec => ABI::V7,
[170](https://landlock.io#170)            Self::LogSubdomains => ABI::V7,
[171](https://landlock.io#171)        }
[172](https://landlock.io#172)    }
[173](https://landlock.io#173)}
[174](https://landlock.io#174)
[175](https://landlock.io#175)#[cfg(test)]
[176](https://landlock.io#176)mod tests {
[177](https://landlock.io#177)    use super::*;
[178](https://landlock.io#178)    use crate::uapi;
[179](https://landlock.io#179)
[180](https://landlock.io#180)    #[test]
[181](https://landlock.io#181)    fn restrict_self_flag_raw_bit() {
[182](https://landlock.io#182)        assert_eq!(
[183](https://landlock.io#183)            RestrictSelfFlag::LogSameExec.raw_bit(),
[184](https://landlock.io#184)            uapi::LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SAME_EXEC_OFF,
[185](https://landlock.io#185)        );
[186](https://landlock.io#186)        assert_eq!(
[187](https://landlock.io#187)            RestrictSelfFlag::LogNewExec.raw_bit(),
[188](https://landlock.io#188)            uapi::LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_NEW_EXEC_ON,
[189](https://landlock.io#189)        );
[190](https://landlock.io#190)        assert_eq!(
[191](https://landlock.io#191)            RestrictSelfFlag::LogSubdomains.raw_bit(),
[192](https://landlock.io#192)            uapi::LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF_LOG_SUBDOMAINS_OFF,
[193](https://landlock.io#193)        );
[194](https://landlock.io#194)    }
[195](https://landlock.io#195)
[196](https://landlock.io#196)    #[test]
[197](https://landlock.io#197)    fn restrict_self_flag_default_value() {
[198](https://landlock.io#198)        assert!(RestrictSelfFlag::LogSameExec.default_value());
[199](https://landlock.io#199)        assert!(!RestrictSelfFlag::LogNewExec.default_value());
[200](https://landlock.io#200)        assert!(RestrictSelfFlag::LogSubdomains.default_value());
[201](https://landlock.io#201)    }
[202](https://landlock.io#202)
[203](https://landlock.io#203)    #[test]
[204](https://landlock.io#204)    fn restrict_self_flag_since() {

[206](https://landlock.io#206)        assert_eq!(RestrictSelfFlag::LogNewExec.since(), ABI::V7);
[207](https://landlock.io#207)        assert_eq!(RestrictSelfFlag::LogSubdomains.since(), ABI::V7);
[208](https://landlock.io#208)    }

# scope.rs - source

Source: https://landlock.io/rust-landlock/src/landlock/scope.rs.html

# landlock/scope.rs

[1](https://landlock.io#1)// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR MIT
[2](https://landlock.io#2)
[3](https://landlock.io#3)use crate::{uapi, Access, ABI};
[4](https://landlock.io#4)use enumflags2::{bitflags, BitFlags};
[5](https://landlock.io#5)
[6](https://landlock.io#6)/// Scope right.
[7](https://landlock.io#7)///
[8](https://landlock.io#8)/// Each variant of `Scope` is a
[9](https://landlock.io#9)/// [scope flag](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/userspace-api/landlock.html#scope-flags).
[10](https://landlock.io#10)/// A set of scopes can be created with [`BitFlags<Scope>`](BitFlags).
[11](https://landlock.io#11)///
[12](https://landlock.io#12)/// # Example
[13](https://landlock.io#13)///
[14](https://landlock.io#14)/// ```
[15](https://landlock.io#15)/// use landlock::{ABI, Access, Scope, BitFlags, make_bitflags};
[16](https://landlock.io#16)///
[17](https://landlock.io#17)/// let signal = Scope::Signal;
[18](https://landlock.io#18)///
[19](https://landlock.io#19)/// let signal_set: BitFlags<Scope> = signal.into();
[20](https://landlock.io#20)///
[21](https://landlock.io#21)/// let signal_uds = make_bitflags!(Scope::{Signal | AbstractUnixSocket});
[22](https://landlock.io#22)///
[23](https://landlock.io#23)/// let scope_v6 = Scope::from_all(ABI::V6);
[24](https://landlock.io#24)///
[25](https://landlock.io#25)/// assert_eq!(signal_uds, scope_v6);
[26](https://landlock.io#26)/// ```
[27](https://landlock.io#27)///
[28](https://landlock.io#28)/// # Warning
[29](https://landlock.io#29)///
[30](https://landlock.io#30)/// To avoid unknown restrictions **don't use `BitFlags::<Scope>::all()` nor `BitFlags::ALL`**,
[31](https://landlock.io#31)/// but use a version you tested and vetted instead,
[32](https://landlock.io#32)/// for instance [`Scope::from_all(ABI::V6)`](Access::from_all).
[33](https://landlock.io#33)/// Direct use of **the [`BitFlags`] API is deprecated**.
[34](https://landlock.io#34)/// See [`ABI`] for the rationale and help to test it.
[35](https://landlock.io#35)#[bitflags]
[36](https://landlock.io#36)#[repr(u64)]
[37](https://landlock.io#37)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[38](https://landlock.io#38)#[non_exhaustive]
[39](https://landlock.io#39)pub enum Scope {
[40](https://landlock.io#40)    /// Restrict from connecting to abstract UNIX sockets created outside the sandbox.
[41](https://landlock.io#41)    AbstractUnixSocket = uapi::LANDLOCK_SCOPE_ABSTRACT_UNIX_SOCKET as u64,
[42](https://landlock.io#42)    /// Restrict from sending signals to processes outside the sandbox.
[43](https://landlock.io#43)    Signal = uapi::LANDLOCK_SCOPE_SIGNAL as u64,
[44](https://landlock.io#44)}
[45](https://landlock.io#45)
[46](https://landlock.io#46)/// # Warning
[47](https://landlock.io#47)///
[48](https://landlock.io#48)/// If `ABI <= ABI::V5`, `Scope::from_all()` returns an empty `BitFlags<AccessScope>`, which
[49](https://landlock.io#49)/// makes `Ruleset::handle_access(AccessScope::from_all(ABI::V5))` return an error.
[50](https://landlock.io#50)impl Access for Scope {
[51](https://landlock.io#51)    fn from_all(abi: ABI) -> BitFlags<Self> {
[52](https://landlock.io#52)        match abi {
[53](https://landlock.io#53)            ABI::Unsupported | ABI::V1 | ABI::V2 | ABI::V3 | ABI::V4 | ABI::V5 => BitFlags::EMPTY,
[54](https://landlock.io#54)            ABI::V6 | ABI::V7 => Scope::AbstractUnixSocket | Scope::Signal,
[55](https://landlock.io#55)        }
[56](https://landlock.io#56)    }
[57](https://landlock.io#57)}

---

[46](#46)fn bit_flags_full_negation() {

[53](#53)
[54](#54)impl<A> TailoredCompatLevel for BitFlags<A> where A: Access {}
[55](#55)
[56](#56)impl<A> TryCompat<A> for BitFlags<A>
[57](#57)where
[58](#58)    A: Access,
[59](#59){
[60](#60)    fn try_compat_inner(&mut self, abi: ABI) -> Result<CompatResult<A>, CompatError<A>> {
[61](#61)        if self.is_empty() {
[62](#62)            Err(AccessError::Empty.into())
[64](#64)        } else if !Self::all().contains(*self) {
[65](#65)            Err(AccessError::Unknown {
[68](#68)                access: *self,
[69](#69)                unknown: *self & full_negation(Self::all()),
[70](#70)            }
[71](#71)            .into())
[72](#72)        } else {
[73](#73)            let compat = *self & A::from_all(abi);
[74](#74)            let ret = if compat.is_empty() {
[75](#75)                Ok(CompatResult::No(
[76](#76)                    AccessError::Incompatible { access: *self }.into(),
[77](#77)                ))
[78](#78)            } else if compat != *self {
[79](#79)                let error = AccessError::PartiallyCompatible {
[80](#80)                    access: *self,
[81](#81)                    incompatible: *self & full_negation(compat),
[82](#82)                }
[83](#83)                .into();
[84](#84)                Ok(CompatResult::Partial(error))
[85](#85)            } else {
[86](#86)                Ok(CompatResult::Full)
[87](#87)            };
[88](#88)            *self = compat;
[89](#89)            ret
[90](#90)        }
[91](#91)    }
[92](#92)}
[93](#93)

[95](#95)fn compat_bit_flags() {
[96](#96)    use crate::ABI;
[97](#97)
[98](#98)    let mut compat: Compatibility = ABI::V1.into();
[99](#99)    assert!(compat.state == CompatState::Init);
[100](#100)
[101](#101)    let ro_access = make_bitflags!(AccessFs::{Execute | ReadFile | ReadDir});
[102](#102)    assert_eq!(
[103](#103)        ro_access,
[104](#104)        ro_access
[105](#105)            .try_compat(compat.abi(), compat.level, &mut compat.state)
[106](#106)            .unwrap()
[107](#107)            .unwrap()
[108](#108)    );
[109](#109)    assert!(compat.state == CompatState::Full);
[110](#110)
[111](#111)    let empty_access = BitFlags::<AccessFs>::empty();
[112](#112)    assert!(matches!(
[113](#113)        empty_access
[114](#114)            .try_compat(compat.abi(), compat.level, &mut compat.state)
[115](#115)            .unwrap_err(),
[116](#116)        CompatError::Access(AccessError::Empty)
[117](#117)    ));
[118](#118)
[119](#119)    let all_unknown_access = unsafe { BitFlags::<AccessFs>::from_bits_unchecked(1 << 63) };
[120](#120)    assert!(matches!(
[121](#121)        all_unknown_access.try_compat(compat.abi(), compat.level, &mut compat.state).unwrap_err(),
[122](#122)        CompatError::Access(AccessError::Unknown { access, unknown }) if access == all_unknown_access && unknown == all_unknown_access
[123](#123)    ));
[124](#124)    assert!(compat.state == CompatState::Dummy);
[126](#126)
[127](#127)    let some_unknown_access = unsafe { BitFlags::<AccessFs>::from_bits_unchecked(1 << 63 | 1) };
[128](#128)    assert!(matches!(
[129](#129)        some_unknown_access.try_compat(compat.abi(), compat.level, &mut compat.state).unwrap_err(),
[130](#130)        CompatError::Access(AccessError::Unknown { access, unknown }) if access == some_unknown_access && unknown == all_unknown_access
[131](#131)    ));
[132](#132)    assert!(compat.state == CompatState::Dummy);
[133](#133)
[134](#134)    compat = ABI::Unsupported.into();
[135](#135)
[136](#136)    assert!(compat.state == CompatState::Init);
[138](#138)
[139](#139)    assert_eq!(
[141](#141)        None,
[142](#142)        ro_access
[143](#143)            .try_compat(compat.abi(), compat.level, &mut compat.state)
[144](#144)            .unwrap()
[145](#145)    );
[146](#146)
[147](#147)    assert!(compat.state == CompatState::No);
[148](#148)
[149](#149)    compat.level = Some(CompatLevel::HardRequirement);
[151](#151)    assert!(matches!(
[152](#152)        ro_access.try_compat(compat.abi(), compat.level, &mut compat.state).unwrap_err(),
[153](#153)        CompatError::Access(AccessError::Incompatible { access }) if access == ro_access
[154](#154)    ));
[155](#155)
[156](#156)    compat = ABI::V1.into();
[157](#157)

[160](#160)

[163](#163)        ro_access,
